nodes.principle: Before execution, remove merge markers, stray prose, duplicated definitions, Markdown/HTML fragments, and other non-Python artifacts.
nodes.condition: After patching, merging, copy-pasting, or generating code.

nodes.principle: Before running a long script, scan it top-to-bottom and ensure every variable, function, class, helper, fold index, and loader is defined before first use.
nodes.condition: Long scripts, merged snippets, multi-stage pipelines, or refactors.

nodes.title: Ensure feature dimension matches model input dimension
nodes.principle: When combining engineered features with a neural network, verify that the number of input features matches the model's expected input dimension (e.g., set num_features to the actual feature count from the pipeline).
nodes.condition: When building hybrid models that concatenate handcrafted features with learned representations.

nodes.title: Fit scaler/vectorizer on training fold only to prevent data leakage
nodes.principle: When using per-fold feature scaling or vectorization, fit the scaler/vectorizer on the training fold only, then transform both training and validation folds. Do not use a pre-fitted scaler from outside the fold.
nodes.condition: When performing cross-validation with feature scaling or vectorization.

nodes.title: Use EfficientNet-B0 with end-to-end fine-tuning and CutMix augmentation for cactus classification
nodes.principle: Use a pretrained EfficientNet-B0 backbone from timm, fine-tune end-to-end with BCEWithLogitsLoss, AdamW optimizer (backbone lr=5e-5, head lr=1e-3), warmup cosine annealing scheduler, CutMix augmentation (50% probability per batch), gradient clipping, and early stopping based on validation AUC.
nodes.condition: When performing binary image classification on the aerial cactus identification dataset with limited data (~14K images) and near-perfect validation AUC is desired.

nodes.title: Use two-stage feature extraction with frozen backbone and MLP classifier for quick baseline
nodes.principle: Use a frozen pretrained backbone (e.g., EfficientNet-B0, ResNet50) to extract features, cache them to disk, then train a small MLP classifier (LayerNorm + 2-3 linear layers with GELU and dropout) on the extracted features using BCEWithLogitsLoss, AdamW optimizer, and ReduceLROnPlateau scheduler.
nodes.condition: When needing a quick baseline or when computational resources are limited (e.g., GPU memory constraints) for aerial cactus identification.

nodes.title: Use handcrafted features combined with CNN features for robust classification
nodes.principle: Extract handcrafted features (color histograms, GLCM texture, LBP, edge features, statistical features, HOG, pooled grayscale) and combine with CNN features from a pretrained EfficientNet-V2-S. Standardize features with StandardScaler and train an MLP classifier with BatchNorm, ReLU, and dropout.
nodes.condition: When deep learning features alone may not capture all relevant patterns, or as a fallback when GPU memory is limited for aerial cactus identification.

nodes.title: Use correct attribute name for SigLIP model config hidden_size
nodes.principle: When accessing the hidden size of a SigLIP model from HuggingFace, use 'hidden_size' (with the typo) instead of 'hidden_size' as the config attribute. Alternatively, access via 'vision_config.hidden_size'.
nodes.condition: When working with SigLIP models (e.g., google/siglip2-so400m-patch16-256) from HuggingFace transformers and needing to get the hidden dimension for classifier head construction.

nodes.title: Use correct DINOv2 input size (518x518) when using vit_large_patch14_dinov2
nodes.principle: When using DINOv2 ViT-Large model from timm (vit_large_patch14_dinov2.lvd142m), resize input images to 518x518 as required by the model. Using smaller sizes (e.g., 224x224) will cause assertion errors.
nodes.condition: When using DINOv2 ViT-Large model from timm and encountering assertion errors about input size mismatch.

nodes.title: Use patch-based extraction with overlapping patches and weighted averaging reconstruction
nodes.principle: Extract overlapping patches (e.g., 64x64 with stride 32) from full-resolution images, train on patches, and reconstruct full images by weighted averaging of overlapping predictions to preserve high-frequency details and avoid resolution loss.
nodes.condition: When working with image denoising tasks where full-image resizing destroys fine details and training data is limited.

nodes.title: Use attention gates in U-Net skip connections for denoising
nodes.principle: Add attention gates (e.g., additive attention) to the skip connections of a U-Net to suppress irrelevant features and enhance important spatial regions, improving denoising quality.
nodes.condition: When building a U-Net for image denoising and standard skip connections propagate noise or irrelevant features.

nodes.title: Use combined loss with RMSE, SSIM, and edge-aware (Sobel) loss for denoising
nodes.principle: Combine RMSE (or MSE), SSIM, and an edge-aware loss (e.g., L1 on Sobel gradients) to balance pixel accuracy, perceptual quality, and edge preservation.
nodes.condition: When training a denoising model and standard L1/L2 loss produces blurry results or loses edge sharpness.

nodes.title: Set DataLoader num_workers=0 to avoid shared memory issues in Kaggle environments
nodes.principle: Set num_workers=0 in DataLoader to avoid shared memory bus errors and worker crashes in restricted environments like Kaggle notebooks.
nodes.condition: When running in a Kaggle or similar environment with limited shared memory and encountering DataLoader worker crashes.

nodes.title: Ensure SSIM loss tensor dtype matches model input dtype under mixed precision
nodes.principle: Create the Gaussian window for SSIM loss with the same dtype as the input tensors (e.g., using .type_as()) to avoid dtype mismatch when using autocast (AMP).
nodes.condition: When using SSIM loss inside an autocast context with mixed precision training.

nodes.title: Use CalibratedClassifierCV with estimator parameter instead of deprecated base_estimator
nodes.principle: When using CalibratedClassifierCV from scikit-learn, pass the base model via the 'estimator' parameter, not the deprecated 'base_estimator' parameter.
nodes.condition: When using CalibratedClassifierCV in scikit-learn versions >=0.24.

nodes.title: Resize images to dimensions that are multiples of the patch size for ViT models
nodes.principle: When using Vision Transformers (e.g., DINOv2 with patch size 14), resize images to dimensions that are multiples of the patch size (e.g., 224, 252) to avoid assertion errors in patch embedding.
nodes.condition: When using ViT models with patch-based embeddings.

nodes.title: Use consistent variable names to avoid NameError from undefined variables
nodes.principle: After feature engineering, ensure the variable names used for training data (e.g., X_train, y_train) match those used in subsequent steps. Avoid referencing variables like X_train_fold that were never defined.
nodes.condition: When building data processing pipelines with multiple steps.

nodes.title: Avoid data leakage by fitting PCA and scalers on training fold only
nodes.principle: When performing dimensionality reduction (PCA) or scaling, fit the transformation on the training fold only, then transform validation and test sets using the fitted object. Do not fit separately on each split.
nodes.condition: When applying PCA or StandardScaler in cross-validation or train/validation splits.

nodes.title: Use early stopping based on validation log loss to prevent overfitting
nodes.principle: Monitor validation log loss each epoch and stop training if it does not improve for a patience number of epochs (e.g., 30), restoring the best model weights.
nodes.condition: When training neural networks on small datasets to avoid overfitting and save time.

nodes.title: Use AdamW optimizer with weight decay for regularization
nodes.principle: Use torch.optim.AdamW with weight_decay=1e-4 to apply decoupled weight decay, improving generalization.
nodes.condition: When training neural networks, especially transformers or MLPs, to regularize weights.

nodes.title: Use gradient clipping to stabilize training and avoid NaN losses
nodes.principle: Apply torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), max_norm=1.0) after loss.backward() to prevent gradient explosion.
nodes.condition: When training deep networks, especially with mixup or complex architectures, to avoid numerical instability.

nodes.title: Avoid using statistical features computed per-sample across the whole dataset before splitting
nodes.principle: Do not compute per-sample statistics (e.g., mean, std, skewness) on the full dataset before train/validation split, as they leak information from other samples. Compute them within each fold's training data only.
nodes.condition: When engineering features that involve per-sample aggregations across the dataset.

nodes.title: Use correct attribute name for HuggingFace model backbone layers
nodes.principle: Access the backbone of a HuggingFace model via the correct attribute (e.g., model.backbone for ModernBERT, model.deberta for DeBERTa) instead of assuming a generic name.
nodes.condition: When building custom models that wrap HuggingFace transformers and need to access the underlying encoder.

nodes.title: Use correct file path for training data and avoid hardcoded local paths
nodes.principle: Use relative paths or environment variables to locate data files (e.g., './input/train.csv') instead of hardcoded absolute paths that may not exist in the execution environment.
nodes.condition: When writing code that will run in different environments (e.g., local vs Kaggle).

nodes.title: Handle missing values per feature group with median imputation to avoid data leakage
nodes.principle: Impute missing values separately for each feature group (margin, shape, texture) using SimpleImputer(strategy='median') fitted on the training fold only, to prevent leakage from validation data.
nodes.condition: When preprocessing tabular data with missing values and natural feature groupings.

nodes.title: Use correct file path for training data
nodes.principle: Read training data from './input/labels.csv' instead of './input/train.csv' when the dataset uses a different filename.
nodes.condition: When the training data file is named 'labels.csv' rather than 'train.csv' in the input directory.

nodes.title: Avoid scaling categorical features with StandardScaler
nodes.principle: Separate categorical features from numerical features before scaling; apply StandardScaler only to numerical columns to prevent negative values in categorical features that LightGBM cannot handle.
nodes.condition: When preprocessing data for tree-based models that treat categorical features as integers.

nodes.title: Exclude non-numeric columns before filling NaNs with median
nodes.principle: When filling missing values with the median, select only numeric columns to avoid TypeError on datetime or object columns.
nodes.condition: When using fillna with median on a DataFrame that contains non-numeric columns.

nodes.title: Compute group statistics on training fold only to prevent data leakage
nodes.principle: Compute location-based group statistics (mean, std, count) only on the training portion after splitting, not on the full dataset before split, to avoid leaking validation information.
nodes.condition: When engineering features that involve aggregating target statistics by location or group.

nodes.title: Use ensemble of raw-fare and log-fare LightGBM models
nodes.principle: Train two LightGBM models: one on raw fare and one on log-transformed fare, then ensemble their predictions (e.g., average) to handle the right-skewed fare distribution.
nodes.condition: When the target variable has a long tail and log transformation helps normalize the distribution.

nodes.title: Freeze backbone and use XGBoost on embeddings to avoid overfitting
nodes.principle: Extract frozen transformer embeddings (e.g., [CLS] token) and train an XGBoost classifier with multi:softprob objective, early stopping, and cross-validation. This avoids fine-tuning instability and overfitting.
nodes.condition: When fine-tuning a large transformer leads to severe overfitting or training instability.

nodes.title: Use ModernBERT-large with proper training regularization
nodes.principle: Fine-tune ModernBERT-large with AdamW (lr=2e-5, weight_decay=0.01), cosine annealing with warm restarts, gradient accumulation (2 steps), gradient clipping (max_norm=1.0), mixed precision, and early stopping (patience=3). Use stratified 85/15 split.
nodes.condition: When using ModernBERT-large for text classification and needing to mitigate overfitting.

nodes.title: Force SentenceTransformer to use CPU to avoid GPU OOM
nodes.principle: Initialize SentenceTransformer with device='cpu' to avoid GPU memory contention when other processes occupy most VRAM.
nodes.condition: When GPU memory is insufficient for loading a SentenceTransformer model due to other processes.

nodes.title: Set DataLoader num_workers=0 to avoid shared memory issues
nodes.principle: Set num_workers=0 in DataLoader (and optionally pin_memory=False) to prevent 'No space left on device' or CUDA bus errors caused by limited shared memory (/dev/shm) in containerized environments.
nodes.condition: When encountering 'Bus error' or 'No space left on device' during DataLoader worker initialization, or when using multiprocessing with limited shared memory.

nodes.title: Disable gradient checkpointing when using gradient accumulation
nodes.principle: Disable gradient_checkpointing_enable() when using gradient accumulation with AMP, as it causes 'Trying to backward through the graph a second time' errors. Instead, reduce batch size to manage memory.
nodes.condition: When training a transformer model with gradient accumulation and mixed precision, and encountering backward pass errors.

nodes.title: Use DeBERTa-v3-large with ensemble of XGBoost and Logistic Regression for best performance
nodes.principle: Fine-tune DeBERTa-v3-large with AdamW, linear warmup, mixed precision, gradient clipping, label smoothing, and early stopping. Combine its embeddings with engineered features (stylometric, readability, POS, n-grams) and train XGBoost and Logistic Regression, then optimize ensemble weights via validation log loss.
nodes.condition: When aiming for top performance on text classification tasks with sufficient GPU memory and training time.

nodes.title: Use DeBERTa-v3-base with multi-task learning and contrastive loss disabled
nodes.principle: Use DeBERTa-v3-base with a classification head, disable contrastive loss to avoid NaN, use AdamW with linear warmup, mixed precision, gradient accumulation, and early stopping. Ensure checkpoint loading uses the exact saved filename.
nodes.condition: When using DeBERTa-v3-base with multi-task learning; disable contrastive loss if numerical instability occurs.

nodes.title: Use ModernBERT-large with proper dropout configuration via config object
nodes.principle: Load ModernBertForSequenceClassification without dropout kwargs, then set dropout via model.config.hidden_dropout_prob and model.config.attention_probs_dropout_prob after loading.
nodes.condition: When using ModernBERT from HuggingFace and needing to adjust dropout probabilities.

nodes.title: Use stratified K-fold cross-validation to ensure balanced validation splits
nodes.principle: Use StratifiedKFold from sklearn to split the training data into folds that preserve the class distribution; use one fold for validation and the rest for training.
nodes.condition: When dealing with imbalanced classification tasks to ensure representative validation metrics.

nodes.title: Use early stopping with patience based on validation loss
nodes.principle: Monitor validation loss and stop training if no improvement for a set number of epochs (e.g., patience=3); save the best model checkpoint.
nodes.condition: When training deep learning models to prevent overfitting and save time.

nodes.title: Use text augmentation (word swaps, punctuation insertion, vowel noise, synonym replacement) to reduce overfitting
nodes.principle: Apply balanced text augmentations to training samples: random word swaps within a window, random punctuation insertion, vowel noise (replace vowels), and synonym replacement using WordNet.
nodes.condition: When training transformer models on small text datasets to improve robustness and reduce overfitting.

nodes.title: Use DeBERTa-v3-large with stylometric features and two-stage fusion with LightGBM
nodes.principle: Combine DeBERTa-v3-large transformer with handcrafted stylometric features (punctuation counts, stopword ratios, archaic/supernatural word counts, sentence length, etc.) and TF-IDF n-grams. Train transformer with label smoothing focal loss, mixed precision, early stopping, and SWA. Then extract pooled embeddings, concatenate with stylometric/TF-IDF features, and train a LightGBM classifier on the combined features.
nodes.condition: When performing author identification on the Spooky Author Identification dataset and aiming for high accuracy with a large transformer model.

nodes.title: Use DeBERTa-v3-large with stylometric features and attention pooling for best performance
nodes.principle: Use DeBERTa-v3-large with multi-layer attention pooling over [CLS] token, residual connections, label smoothing cross-entropy loss, mixed precision (AMP), AdamW optimizer, linear warmup scheduler, and early stopping. Incorporate 30 stylometric features (word/sentence counts, punctuation density, part-of-speech ratios).
nodes.condition: When aiming for the best possible validation log loss (around 0.30) on Spooky Author Identification with sufficient GPU memory.

nodes.title: Use RoBERTa-base with label smoothing and ensemble of two models
nodes.principle: Train two RoBERTa-base models with different random seeds, using label smoothing cross-entropy loss, AdamW optimizer, linear warmup scheduler, mixed precision, and early stopping. Average softmax outputs of the two models for final predictions.
nodes.condition: When using RoBERTa-base for Spooky Author Identification and wanting a simple ensemble to improve robustness.

nodes.title: Use DeBERTa-v3-small with multi-head attention pooling and multi-sample dropout
nodes.principle: Use DeBERTa-v3-small with a multi-head attention pooling layer replacing CLS pooling, multi-sample dropout (4 forward passes averaged during training), layer-wise learning rate decay, label smoothing loss, gradient accumulation, mixed precision (AMP), and early stopping. Combine with 120 linguistic/stylistic features and TF-IDF vectors.
nodes.condition: When GPU memory is limited but a transformer model is desired for Spooky Author Identification; DeBERTa-v3-small fits in memory.

nodes.title: Use BERT-base-cased with gated fusion of stylometric features and learnable layer pooling
nodes.principle: Use BERT-base-cased with learnable weighted layer pooling (including stochastic depth during training), mean+max pooling, separate projections for BERT and 21 stylometric features (word/sentence length statistics, punctuation rates, author-specific keyword scores), a gating network to fuse both representations, and a multi-layer classifier. Train with CrossEntropyLoss, AdamW optimizer, cosine schedule with warmup, gradient accumulation, mixed precision, and early stopping.
nodes.condition: When combining BERT with handcrafted stylometric features for Spooky Author Identification and wanting a learnable fusion mechanism.

nodes.title: Handle None pooler in RoBERTa for layer grouping
nodes.principle: When implementing gradual unfreezing or discriminative learning rates for RoBERTa, check if `model.roberta.pooler` is None before accessing its parameters. If None, exclude it from the parameter groups.
nodes.condition: When using HuggingFace RoBERTaForSequenceClassification and trying to group layers by name (e.g., for different learning rates).

nodes.title: Use TF-IDF with handcrafted features and Logistic Regression as a strong baseline for text classification
nodes.principle: Combine TF-IDF vectorization (max 50k features, 1-3 ngrams) with handcrafted statistical features (character/word/sentence counts, punctuation counts, quote density, capital ratio, unique word ratio, stopword ratio). Scale features with StandardScaler and concatenate via sparse hstack. Train a multinomial Logistic Regression (C=4.0, solver='saga') with 5-fold stratified cross-validation. This provides a robust baseline that avoids overfitting on small datasets.
nodes.condition: When starting a text classification task with limited data and need a quick, non-overfitting baseline.

nodes.title: Set DataLoader drop_last=True to avoid BatchNorm issues with small last batch
nodes.principle: When using BatchNorm layers, set drop_last=True in the DataLoader to drop the incomplete last batch, preventing ValueError due to single-sample batch.
nodes.condition: When training neural networks with BatchNorm and the dataset size is not a multiple of the batch size.

nodes.title: Escape regex special characters in str.count for parenthesis counting
nodes.principle: When counting parentheses in text using str.count, use literal strings (e.g., '(' and ')') as str.count does not interpret regex. However, if using regex functions like re.findall, escape parentheses with backslash. In pandas, str.count with '(' works correctly as it treats the argument as a literal string, not a regex pattern.
nodes.condition: When counting special characters like parentheses in text data using pandas str.count.

nodes.title: Combine stylometric features with transformer via cross-attention fusion
nodes.principle: Engineer stylometric features (character/word counts, punctuation ratios, readability scores, etc.) and fuse them with transformer embeddings using a cross-attention module with gating to improve author identification.
nodes.condition: When building a model for author identification where stylistic cues are important.

nodes.title: Ensure attention mask shape matches multi-head attention expectations
nodes.principle: When using nn.MultiheadAttention with num_heads > 1, expand the attention mask to shape [batch_size * num_heads, seq_len, seq_len] instead of [batch_size, seq_len, seq_len].
nodes.condition: When implementing custom attention modules with nn.MultiheadAttention and num_heads > 1.

nodes.title: Download all required NLTK resources before tokenization
nodes.principle: Download all necessary NLTK resources (punkt, averaged_perceptron_tagger, etc.) using nltk.download() before calling tokenization or POS tagging functions, and handle missing resources gracefully.
nodes.condition: When using NLTK for text preprocessing in a script that may run in a fresh environment.

nodes.title: Use smaller negative value for masked_fill in float16 to avoid overflow
nodes.principle: In attention pooling or similar modules, when using masked_fill with a large negative value (e.g., -1e9) under mixed precision (float16), replace with a smaller negative value like -1e4 that can be represented in float16 without overflow.
nodes.condition: When using mixed precision training (autocast) and masked_fill with a large negative value causes overflow in float16.

nodes.title: Combine engineered features with transformer embeddings for hybrid model
nodes.principle: Extract handcrafted features (text statistics, n-grams, POS, sentiment, author-specific vocabulary) and concatenate them with transformer [CLS] embeddings or use them as input to a secondary model (e.g., LightGBM) for ensemble.
nodes.condition: When building a strong classifier for text classification tasks with limited data.

nodes.title: Use single-phase training instead of progressive unfreezing to avoid OOM
nodes.principle: Train the entire model from the start with a lower learning rate for the backbone, avoiding progressive unfreezing which can cause memory spikes when unfreezing layers.
nodes.condition: When progressive unfreezing leads to CUDA OOM at later stages due to increased memory usage from unfrozen layers.

nodes.title: Reduce gradient accumulation steps to lower peak memory
nodes.principle: Use fewer gradient accumulation steps (e.g., 2 instead of 4) to reduce peak GPU memory usage during training.
nodes.condition: When CUDA OOM occurs during backward pass with gradient accumulation enabled.

nodes.title: Avoid multi-scale convolutional layers that increase memory footprint
nodes.principle: Use a simpler classification head (e.g., mean pooling + linear layer) instead of multi-scale Conv1D blocks to reduce model memory usage.
nodes.condition: When the model architecture includes memory-intensive components like multi-scale convolutions and CUDA OOM occurs.

nodes.title: Use MLP with TF-IDF and stylometric features for text classification baseline
nodes.principle: Extract stylometric features (word/sentence length statistics, punctuation ratios, POS counts), character n-gram TF-IDF (2-5), word n-gram TF-IDF (1-3), scale with StandardScaler, and train a 3-layer MLP (512-256-128) with BatchNorm, GELU, dropout, AdamW, cosine annealing warm restarts, mixed precision, label smoothing, and early stopping.
nodes.condition: When building a strong non-transformer baseline for text classification tasks with limited data.

nodes.title: Use handcrafted stylometric features for authorship attribution
nodes.principle: Extract 26 stylometric features including word-level statistics (avg word length, sentence length), punctuation density, stopword ratio, type-token ratio, readability indices (Coleman-Lieu, Flesch), lexical richness measures, and normalize with StandardScaler.
nodes.condition: When performing authorship attribution or style-based text classification to capture writing style signals.

nodes.title: Use XGBoost with handcrafted stylometric features and Sentence-BERT embeddings for text classification
nodes.principle: Combine 32 handcrafted stylometric features (text statistics, punctuation ratios, POS-like patterns, emotional tone indicators) with 384-dimensional Sentence-BERT embeddings (all-MiniLM-L6-v2). Scale features with StandardScaler. Train XGBoost with multi:softprob objective, max_depth=6, learning_rate=0.1, n_estimators=500, subsample=0.8, colsample_bytree=0.8, early_stopping_rounds=50, using 5-fold stratified cross-validation.
nodes.condition: When building a strong baseline for text classification with limited GPU resources or avoiding GPU OOM.

nodes.title: Escape regex metacharacters in pandas str.count to avoid re.error
nodes.principle: When using pandas str.count on text columns, escape regex metacharacters (e.g., parentheses, dots) using re.escape or by passing regex=False parameter to avoid re.error.
nodes.condition: When counting literal characters like parentheses or dots in pandas string columns.

nodes.title: Use correct attribute path for ModernBERT backbone layers
nodes.principle: ModernBERT uses 'encoder.layer' (not 'transformer.layers' or 'encoder.layer' may vary; check model config). Access layers via model.backbone.encoder.layer or model.encoder.layer depending on the model wrapper.
nodes.condition: When unfreezing specific layers of a ModernBERT model from HuggingFace.

nodes.title: Ensure test features dimension matches model input dimension
nodes.principle: When creating test dataset tensors, verify that the number of test samples matches across all feature arrays (e.g., test_features, test_input_ids). Avoid computing test features on combined train+test data.
nodes.condition: When building hybrid models that combine engineered features with transformer inputs.

nodes.title: Use direct feature concatenation instead of complex cross-attention fusion
nodes.principle: Concatenate the [CLS] token embedding with projected engineered features (e.g., stylometric, TF-IDF) and pass through a simple MLP classifier. Avoid multi-head cross-attention or gated fusion mechanisms that introduce instability and overfitting.
nodes.condition: When combining transformer text embeddings with handcrafted features for classification, and simpler fusion yields better validation loss.

nodes.title: Use DistilBERT with differential learning rates and gradual unfreezing
nodes.principle: Freeze the first 4 layers of DistilBERT, fine-tune layers 4-5 with a lower learning rate (e.g., 2e-5), and use a higher learning rate (e.g., 2e-4) for the classification head. Optionally use two-phase training: freeze all transformer layers first, then unfreeze gradually.
nodes.condition: When using DistilBERT as the transformer backbone for text classification to balance feature reuse and task adaptation.

nodes.title: Use smaller model variant (DistilBERT) to avoid CUDA OOM
nodes.principle: Replace a large transformer (e.g., DeBERTa-v3-large) with a smaller variant (e.g., DistilBERT-base) to reduce GPU memory usage and avoid out-of-memory errors.
nodes.condition: When the dataset is small or GPU memory is limited, and a smaller model still achieves competitive performance.

nodes.title: Ensure model forward method returns logits consistently
nodes.principle: Ensure the model's forward method returns logits as a tensor directly, or as an object with a .logits attribute, consistently across all code paths. Avoid returning tuples or dictionaries that may break downstream loss computation.
nodes.condition: When defining custom PyTorch models to be used with standard loss functions.

nodes.title: Avoid calling scaler.unscale_ twice per step
nodes.principle: Call scaler.unscale_(optimizer) only once per gradient accumulation step, and not before FGM attack if scaler.step will call it automatically, to prevent RuntimeError.
nodes.condition: When using GradScaler with adversarial training (FGM) and gradient accumulation.

nodes.title: Use freeze-thaw fine-tuning with focal loss and attention pooling to stabilize DeBERTa training
nodes.principle: Freeze the encoder for the first 3 epochs, then unfreeze with differential learning rates; use focal loss and multi-head attention pooling to reduce overfitting and improve generalization.
nodes.condition: When fine-tuning DeBERTa-v3-large on a small dataset to prevent overfitting and stabilize training.

nodes.title: Avoid random truncation strategies that corrupt sentence structure
nodes.principle: Use consistent truncation (e.g., 'head' or 'tail') instead of random truncation to prevent tokenization issues and numerical instability that lead to NaN predictions.
nodes.condition: When training transformer models for text classification with truncation strategies per fold.

nodes.title: Use logistic regression blender on XGBoost and logistic regression predictions
nodes.principle: Train a final logistic regression model on the out-of-fold predictions of XGBoost and logistic regression meta-models to blend them for improved log loss.
nodes.condition: When ensembling multiple models for classification.

nodes.title: Use consistent truncation strategy across all folds to avoid data leakage
nodes.principle: Apply the same truncation strategy (e.g., 'head') for all folds to ensure consistent input representation and prevent numerical instability.
nodes.condition: When performing cross-validation with transformer models.

nodes.title: Use stratified train/validation split to maintain class distribution
nodes.principle: Use sklearn.model_selection.StratifiedShuffleSplit or StratifiedKFold with random_state to split data while preserving class proportions, preventing data leakage and ensuring balanced validation.
nodes.condition: When performing supervised classification with imbalanced or small datasets.

nodes.title: Ensure stylometric feature array index matches DataFrame index after train/validation split
nodes.principle: When creating stylometric feature arrays from a DataFrame, use .iloc or .loc with the validation indices derived from the DataFrame's index, or reset the DataFrame index before splitting to avoid index mismatch. Alternatively, fit the feature scaler on the training fold and transform both folds using integer-based indexing.
nodes.condition: When using sklearn's train_test_split or StratifiedKFold on a DataFrame and then indexing a separate numpy array of stylometric features with the resulting indices, ensure the array length matches the DataFrame length and indices are aligned.

nodes.title: Use handcrafted stylometric, readability, and POS approximation features for author identification
nodes.principle: Extract features including punctuation ratios, word diversity, archaic/emotional word counts, Flesch Reading Ease, ARI, syllable counts, and POS-tag approximations via suffix matching. Standardize and variance-filter before use.
nodes.condition: When performing authorship attribution or text classification where writing style is discriminative.

nodes.title: Use ReduceLROnPlateau scheduler for transformer fine-tuning to stabilize training
nodes.principle: Use ReduceLROnPlateau scheduler that reduces learning rate when validation loss plateaus. Combine with linear warmup and AdamW optimizer.
nodes.condition: When fine-tuning a transformer model and needing adaptive learning rate adjustment based on validation performance.

nodes.title: Avoid overlapping parameter groups in optimizer construction
nodes.principle: Ensure that parameter groups for differential learning rates are mutually exclusive. Use set operations to verify no parameter appears in multiple groups before creating the optimizer.
nodes.condition: When constructing an optimizer with multiple parameter groups for differential learning rates.

nodes.title: Use correct attribute path for HuggingFace model layers
nodes.principle: For DistilRoBERTa, access layers via model.roberta.encoder.layer. For DeBERTa-v3, access via model.deberta.encoder.layer. Verify the correct attribute path for the specific model variant.
nodes.condition: When accessing intermediate layers of HuggingFace transformer models for custom operations.

nodes.title: Use ensemble of DeBERTa-v3-large, XGBoost, and Logistic Regression with optimized weights
nodes.principle: Train DeBERTa-v3-large with label smoothing (0.1), linear warmup scheduler, gradient accumulation (4 steps), and mixed precision. Extract pooled embeddings and combine with handcrafted stylometric/readability/POS features. Train XGBoost and Logistic Regression on concatenated features. Optimize ensemble weights via grid search (e.g., DeBERTa=0.1, XGBoost=0.8, LogisticRegression=0.1) to minimize validation log-loss.
nodes.condition: When aiming for best performance on spooky-author-identification with sufficient compute (GPU memory for DeBERTa-v3-large) and time (3+ hours).

nodes.title: Avoid complex multi-task losses (contrastive, center loss) that cause dimension mismatches
nodes.principle: Stick to simple cross-entropy or focal loss with label smoothing. If using additional losses, ensure embedding dimensions match exactly (e.g., projection head output dim equals centers dim).
nodes.condition: When designing loss functions for transformer-based classifiers; complex losses often introduce bugs and may not improve performance.

nodes.title: Use torch.save(model.state_dict(), ...) and load with model.load_state_dict(...) to avoid pooler mismatch
nodes.principle: Save only the state_dict (not the full model) and load it into the model instance. Ensure the model architecture (including pooler) is consistent between save and load. For DeBERTa, avoid expecting a pooler layer if using AutoModelForSequenceClassification.
nodes.condition: When checkpointing and reloading transformer models; saving full model can cause key mismatches if architecture changes.

nodes.title: Use gradient accumulation with mixed precision and gradient clipping
nodes.principle: Accumulate gradients over multiple steps, use AMP for memory efficiency, and clip gradients to stabilize training.
nodes.condition: When training large transformers with limited GPU memory.

nodes.title: Use Logistic Regression as quick validation baseline
nodes.principle: Train a Logistic Regression on TF-IDF and handcrafted features to get a quick performance estimate before deep learning.
nodes.condition: When starting a new text classification task.

nodes.title: Use handcrafted stylometric, readability, and POS-approximation features for author identification
nodes.principle: Extract 30+ stylometric features (punctuation ratios, word length stats, function word counts, archaic/emotional word ratios), 4 readability features (Flesch score, ARI, syllables, complex word ratio), and 5 POS-approximation features (noun/verb/adj/adv ratios via suffix matching) as additional inputs to XGBoost or ensemble.
nodes.condition: When working on authorship attribution tasks with limited training data.

nodes.title: Optimize ensemble weights via grid search on validation log loss
nodes.principle: After training individual models, perform a grid search over weight combinations (e.g., step 0.05) to minimize validation log loss, then apply the optimal weights to test predictions.
nodes.condition: When combining multiple models (transformer, XGBoost, logistic regression) into an ensemble.

nodes.title: Use semi-supervised test set augmentation for n-gram features
nodes.principle: Append a fraction (e.g., 10%) of test samples with pseudo-labels to the training set before extracting n-gram TF-IDF features, improving domain adaptation for XGBoost.
nodes.condition: When n-gram features show distribution shift between train and test sets.

nodes.title: Use logistic regression as a quick validation baseline and ensemble component
nodes.principle: Train a multinomial logistic regression on sparse n-gram features (e.g., TF-IDF) as a fast baseline. Include its predictions in the final ensemble, often with a small weight.
nodes.condition: When building an ensemble for text classification; logistic regression provides a simple, interpretable model that captures linear patterns.

nodes.title: Ensure SigLIP model receives both pixel_values and input_ids for forward pass
nodes.principle: When using a multimodal SigLIP model (vision-language), provide both pixel_values and input_ids to the forward method. For vision-only tasks, use a vision-only backbone (e.g., from timm) or extract image features using the vision encoder separately.
nodes.condition: When using SigLIP2 or similar vision-language models for image-only classification tasks, as they expect both image and text inputs.

nodes.title: Ensure test image paths are correctly handled during pseudo-labeling retraining
nodes.principle: When adding pseudo-labeled test samples to the training set, ensure the dataset loader can access images from both train and test directories. Either copy test images to the train directory or modify the dataset to accept a list of image paths with corresponding directories.
nodes.condition: When implementing pseudo-labeling that adds test samples to the training set for retraining, to avoid FileNotFoundError due to incorrect image directory.

nodes.title: Use correct classifier head dimensions for EfficientNet-V2-S backbone
nodes.principle: When replacing the classifier head of EfficientNet-V2-S from timm, use the backbone's in_features attribute (e.g., 1280) for the first linear layer. Avoid adding extra pooling layers as the backbone already includes adaptive average pooling.
nodes.condition: When customizing the classifier head of EfficientNet-V2-S from timm and encountering shape mismatches due to incorrect in_features.

nodes.title: Handle DINOv2 forward_features output correctly (tensor, not dict)
nodes.principle: When using DINOv2 models from timm, the forward_features method returns a tensor (the CLS token) directly, not a dictionary. Access the output as a tensor without indexing by key.
nodes.condition: When using DINOv2 models from timm and encountering IndexError when trying to access output['x_norm_clstoken'].

nodes.title: Use curriculum learning with multi-scale patches (large then small) for denoising
nodes.principle: Train initially on larger patches (e.g., 128x128) to learn global context, then switch to smaller patches (e.g., 64x64) to refine fine details, using a curriculum learning schedule.
nodes.condition: When training a denoising model and the model struggles to capture both global structure and fine details simultaneously.

nodes.title: Resize images to dimensions that are multiples of the patch size for ViT-based models
nodes.principle: Ensure input image dimensions are exact multiples of the ViT patch size (e.g., 14 for DINOv2) by resizing to a compatible size (e.g., 546x546) to avoid assertion errors in patch embedding.
nodes.condition: When using a Vision Transformer (ViT) model that requires input dimensions divisible by the patch size.

nodes.title: Use DINOv2 ViT-L/14 with gated multimodal fusion for leaf classification
nodes.principle: Use DINOv2 ViT-L/14 as frozen image feature extractor (1024-dim), engineer extensive tabular features (raw values, per-group statistics, cross-group interactions, PCA), and train a multimodal classifier with separate projectors for tabular and image modalities, a learnable gating fusion mechanism, and a classifier head with label smoothing cross-entropy loss. Use AdamW optimizer with cosine annealing scheduler, mixed precision training, and early stopping.
nodes.condition: When performing leaf species classification with both tabular and image data, and aiming for high accuracy with limited training data.

nodes.title: Use extensive tabular feature engineering with statistical summaries, ratios, correlations, and PCA for leaf classification
nodes.principle: Engineer tabular features from margin/shape/texture groups: per-group statistics (mean, std, min, max, skew, kurtosis, quartiles, IQR, range, CV), ratio features, cross-group correlations, PCA per group (8 components) and difference PCA (5 components). Fit all transformations on the training fold only to prevent leakage.
nodes.condition: When working with leaf classification tabular data containing margin, shape, and texture features.

nodes.title: Use ensemble of XGBoost, MLP on image features, and Logistic Regression with optimized weights
nodes.principle: Train three models: XGBoost on engineered tabular features, an MLP on SigLIP2 image embeddings, and a Logistic Regression with polynomial features. Optimize ensemble weights via grid search on validation log loss to minimize the metric.
nodes.condition: When combining tabular and image features for leaf classification and seeking robust generalization through ensembling.

nodes.title: Use SigLIP2 vision_model subcomponent for image-only feature extraction
nodes.principle: When using SigLIP2 for image-only tasks, access the vision model via model_siglip.vision_model instead of the full model, to avoid requiring text inputs.
nodes.condition: When extracting image features from SigLIP2 without text inputs.

nodes.title: Avoid CatBoost random_seed and random_state conflict
nodes.principle: When using CatBoostClassifier, do not set both 'random_seed' and 'random_state' parameters simultaneously. Use only 'random_state' for consistency.
nodes.condition: When configuring CatBoost models in scikit-learn pipelines.

nodes.title: Use test-time augmentation (TTA) with small noise for inference
nodes.principle: During inference, generate multiple perturbed versions of each test sample (e.g., add Gaussian noise to features) and average the predictions to improve robustness and reduce variance.
nodes.condition: When model is sensitive to input perturbations and you want to stabilize predictions.

nodes.title: Use CosineAnnealingLR scheduler with warmup for stable training
nodes.principle: Implement a cosine annealing learning rate schedule with a linear warmup phase (e.g., 5 epochs) to gradually increase LR then decay, helping convergence.
nodes.condition: When training neural networks with AdamW optimizer, especially for fine-tuning or from scratch on small datasets.

nodes.title: Avoid data leakage by fitting scalers and PCA on training fold only
nodes.principle: Within each cross-validation fold, fit StandardScaler and PCA exclusively on the training subset, then transform both train and validation subsets. Never use the full dataset before splitting.
nodes.condition: When performing feature engineering or dimensionality reduction in a cross-validation setting.

nodes.title: Ensure loss tensor is scalar before calling backward()
nodes.principle: When using mixup or custom loss functions, ensure the loss tensor is reduced to a scalar (e.g., by calling .mean()) before calling loss.backward(), otherwise PyTorch raises 'grad can be implicitly created only for scalar outputs'.
nodes.condition: When implementing custom loss functions or mixup augmentation that may produce non-scalar losses.

nodes.title: Pass categorical features as column indices to LightGBM when using numpy arrays
nodes.principle: When providing data as numpy arrays to LightGBM, specify categorical features as a list of column indices (integers) rather than feature names, and avoid including categorical_feature in the params dict.
nodes.condition: When using LightGBM with numpy array input and categorical features.

nodes.title: Use .loc instead of .iloc for boolean indexing
nodes.principle: When filtering a DataFrame with a boolean mask, use .loc[mask] instead of .iloc[mask] because .iloc does not support boolean indexing.
nodes.condition: When applying a boolean mask to select rows from a pandas DataFrame.

nodes.title: Use XGBoost with standard squared error objective for fare prediction
nodes.principle: Use 'reg:squarederror' objective for XGBoost instead of 'reg:pseudohubererror' to avoid divergence, and clip predictions before applying expm1 to prevent overflow.
nodes.condition: When training XGBoost for regression on log-transformed fare with large dataset.

nodes.title: Process validation data in batches to avoid CUDA OOM
nodes.principle: When validating a neural network on a large dataset, process validation data in batches (same as training) instead of a single forward pass to avoid out-of-memory errors.
nodes.condition: When using GPU for neural network inference on a large validation set.

nodes.title: Use CrossEntropyLoss with label_smoothing instead of LabelSmoothingCrossEntropy
nodes.principle: Use torch.nn.CrossEntropyLoss with the label_smoothing parameter instead of importing LabelSmoothingCrossEntropy from transformers, which may not be available.
nodes.condition: When label smoothing is needed and the transformers library version may not support LabelSmoothingCrossEntropy.

nodes.title: Use smaller SentenceTransformer model to avoid CUDA OOM
nodes.principle: Replace large SentenceTransformer models (e.g., all-mpnet-base-v2, 768-dim) with smaller ones (e.g., all-MiniLM-L6-v2, 384-dim) to reduce GPU memory usage and avoid CUDA out-of-memory errors during embedding extraction.
nodes.condition: When extracting Sentence-BERT embeddings on a GPU with limited free memory due to other processes.

nodes.title: Pass model config via DistilBertConfig object
nodes.principle: When modifying dropout probabilities for DistilBERT, create a DistilBertConfig object with desired parameters and pass it to from_pretrained via config=config, not as direct keyword arguments.
nodes.condition: When customizing dropout or other config parameters for DistilBERT model.

nodes.title: Use DeBERTa-v3-small with gradient checkpointing disabled and reduced batch size
nodes.principle: Use DeBERTa-v3-small instead of large/base to fit in GPU memory. Disable gradient checkpointing to avoid backward pass errors, and reduce batch size to manage memory.
nodes.condition: When fine-tuning a DeBERTa model on a GPU with limited memory and encountering OOM or gradient checkpointing conflicts.

nodes.title: Use RoBERTa-base with proper initialization (avoid passing dropout directly to from_pretrained)
nodes.principle: When using RobertaForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained(), do not pass 'dropout' or 'attention_dropout' as keyword arguments; instead, configure dropout after loading the model by modifying model.config.
nodes.condition: When initializing a RoBERTa model for sequence classification.

nodes.title: Use DistilBERT with partial freezing and label smoothing for moderate performance
nodes.principle: Freeze first 4 of 6 transformer layers, use CrossEntropyLoss with label_smoothing=0.1, AdamW optimizer, cosine scheduler with warmup, gradient accumulation, and mixed precision. Train with early stopping.
nodes.condition: When using DistilBERT for text classification with limited compute and moderate accuracy requirements.

nodes.title: Use MLP with engineered features and Sentence-BERT embeddings for baseline
nodes.principle: Extract lexical, syntactic, stopword, structural, and char TF-IDF features, combine with Sentence-BERT embeddings (all-mpnet-base-v2), and train a 3-layer MLP with LayerNorm, dropout, and AdamW. Use cosine annealing scheduler and early stopping.
nodes.condition: When building a strong baseline without fine-tuning a large transformer.

nodes.title: Use CosineAnnealingWarmRestarts scheduler with linear warmup for transformer fine-tuning
nodes.principle: Use a cosine annealing scheduler with linear warmup (e.g., warmup_steps=500) and restarts (T_0=10, T_mult=2) to improve generalization and escape plateaus.
nodes.condition: When fine-tuning transformer models for text classification.

nodes.title: Use label smoothing in CrossEntropyLoss to prevent overconfidence
nodes.principle: Set CrossEntropyLoss with label_smoothing=0.1 to penalize overconfident predictions and improve generalization.
nodes.condition: When training classification models prone to overfitting, especially with large transformers.

nodes.title: Use mixed precision training with GradScaler for memory efficiency
nodes.principle: Enable automatic mixed precision (AMP) with torch.cuda.amp.autocast and GradScaler to reduce GPU memory usage and speed up training without significant accuracy loss.
nodes.condition: When training large transformer models on GPU with limited memory.

nodes.title: Use gradient accumulation to simulate larger batch size
nodes.principle: Accumulate gradients over multiple forward/backward passes (e.g., 2 steps) before performing an optimizer step, with effective batch size = per_device_batch_size * accumulation_steps, to increase batch size without extra memory.
nodes.condition: When GPU memory is insufficient or limited for desired batch size during transformer training.

nodes.title: Use Stochastic Weight Averaging (SWA) to improve generalization
nodes.principle: After training, average model weights from the last few epochs (e.g., last 5) using SWA to obtain a smoother solution that generalizes better.
nodes.condition: When fine-tuning transformers and validation loss plateaus or oscillates.

nodes.title: Use DistilBERT with focal loss and gradient accumulation for moderate performance
nodes.principle: Use DistilBERT as the base model with focal loss (gamma=2.0), AdamW optimizer, cosine schedule with warmup, gradient accumulation (steps=2), mixed precision training, and early stopping (patience=3). Use stratified train/validation split (80/20).
nodes.condition: When a faster, lighter model is needed for Spooky Author Identification and a moderate validation log loss (around 0.37-0.38) is acceptable.

nodes.title: Import AutoModelForSequenceClassification when using AutoModel classes
nodes.principle: When using HuggingFace AutoModel classes, ensure that `AutoModelForSequenceClassification` is imported from `transformers` if the code uses it. A common mistake is to only import `AutoTokenizer` and `AutoConfig`.
nodes.condition: When writing scripts that use HuggingFace AutoModelForSequenceClassification.

nodes.title: Use ModernBERT-large with TF-IDF and handcrafted features in a hybrid model for best performance
nodes.principle: Combine ModernBERT-large fine-tuning with TF-IDF features (character 2-5-grams and word 1-3-grams) and handcrafted lexical/structural features (e.g., punctuation density, stop word rates, author-specific vocabulary counts). Fit TF-IDF vectorizers and StandardScaler per fold to prevent leakage. Use 3-fold stratified cross-validation, AdamW optimizer, cosine LR schedule with warmup, gradient accumulation, mixed precision, and early stopping. This achieves log-loss around 0.35.
nodes.condition: When the highest possible performance is required on a text classification task with sufficient computational resources.

nodes.title: Avoid variable name collision between GradScaler and StandardScaler
nodes.principle: Do not reuse the variable name 'scaler' for both torch.cuda.amp.GradScaler and sklearn.preprocessing.StandardScaler. Use distinct names to avoid AttributeError when calling .transform() on the wrong object.
nodes.condition: When using both mixed precision training (GradScaler) and feature scaling (StandardScaler) in the same script.

nodes.title: Use DeBERTa-v3-small with differential learning rates and gradient clipping to avoid NaN predictions
nodes.principle: Use a smaller transformer variant (e.g., DeBERTa-v3-small) with differential learning rates (backbone 2e-5, classifier 5e-5), cosine schedule with warmup, gradient clipping, and early stopping to prevent numerical instability and overfitting.
nodes.condition: When training a transformer model on a small text classification dataset and encountering NaN predictions or overfitting.

nodes.title: Use two-phase training: freeze backbone then fine-tune with discriminative learning rates
nodes.principle: Train in two phases: Phase 1 freezes the transformer backbone and trains only the classification head and auxiliary modules; Phase 2 unfreezes the backbone (or LoRA adapters) with a lower learning rate to prevent overfitting and instability.
nodes.condition: When fine-tuning a large transformer on a small dataset to avoid overfitting and gradient instability.

nodes.title: Use multi-scale convolutional block and attention pooling on transformer hidden states
nodes.principle: Apply multiple parallel 1D convolutions with different kernel sizes (e.g., 2,3,5,7) followed by adaptive max pooling and attention pooling on transformer hidden states to capture multi-scale features before classification.
nodes.condition: When designing a custom head for a transformer model to improve sequence representation.

nodes.title: Reduce model size or batch size to avoid CUDA OOM
nodes.principle: Use a smaller model variant (e.g., DeBERTa-v3-small instead of base) or reduce batch size to fit GPU memory. Disable gradient checkpointing if it conflicts with gradient accumulation.
nodes.condition: When training a transformer model on a GPU and encountering CUDA out-of-memory errors during forward/backward passes.

nodes.title: Avoid rebuilding optimizer mid-training to prevent memory leaks
nodes.principle: Do not recreate the optimizer or scheduler during training (e.g., at progressive unfreezing stages). Instead, update parameter groups in-place or use a single optimizer throughout.
nodes.condition: When implementing progressive unfreezing or multi-stage training that would normally require rebuilding the optimizer.

nodes.title: Use DistilBERT with label smoothing and warmup cosine annealing for text classification
nodes.principle: Use DistilBERT-base-uncased with a classification head, AdamW optimizer (2e-5 for BERT, 1e-3 for head), linear warmup for 10% of epochs, cosine annealing scheduler, mixed precision (AMP), gradient clipping (norm=1.0), label smoothing (0.1), and early stopping (patience=3) to achieve strong validation log loss.
nodes.condition: When performing text classification on a small-to-medium dataset (e.g., author identification) and seeking a strong transformer baseline.

nodes.title: Use correct attribute path for DeBERTa-v3-large backbone layers
nodes.principle: When accessing encoder layers of DeBERTa-v3-large via AutoModel, use model.backbone.encoder.layer (not model.backbone.deberta.encoder.layer) because AutoModel returns the backbone directly.
nodes.condition: When fine-tuning DeBERTa-v3-large and needing to access specific encoder layers for partial unfreezing.

nodes.title: Avoid using external GloVe embeddings that may not be available
nodes.principle: Instead of relying on external GloVe embedding files (e.g., glove.6B.300d.txt) or torch.hub/torchtext GloVe loaders, use trainable random embeddings with Xavier initialization to avoid FileNotFoundError or download failures.
nodes.condition: When building text classification models in environments where pre-trained embeddings may not be pre-downloaded or accessible.

nodes.title: Use DistilRoBERTa with 5-fold cross-validation and cosine warmup scheduler for text classification
nodes.principle: Use DistilRoBERTa (distilroberta-base) with a classification head. Train with 5-fold stratified cross-validation, AdamW optimizer (learning_rate=2e-5), cosine schedule with warmup (warmup_steps=500), gradient accumulation (2 steps), mixed precision via Accelerator, early stopping (patience=3) based on validation log loss. Tokenize with max_length=256.
nodes.condition: When fine-tuning a transformer for text classification with moderate compute resources.

nodes.title: Pass all required arguments to function calls to avoid TypeError
nodes.principle: Ensure that when calling a function, all required positional arguments are provided. Check function signature and call site for missing arguments.
nodes.condition: When defining and calling custom functions in Python.

nodes.title: Use integer-encoded labels in PyTorch Dataset, not raw strings
nodes.principle: When creating a PyTorch Dataset for classification, ensure labels are integer-encoded (e.g., via LabelEncoder) before passing to the dataset, not raw string labels.
nodes.condition: When building a PyTorch Dataset for classification tasks with string labels.

nodes.title: Use two-phase training with frozen backbone then full fine-tuning
nodes.principle: Train in two phases: Phase 1 freezes all transformer layers and trains only the classification head for a few epochs; Phase 2 unfreezes selected layers (e.g., last 4-8) and fine-tunes with a lower learning rate. Use separate optimizers or parameter groups with differential learning rates.
nodes.condition: When fine-tuning a large pretrained transformer on a small dataset to prevent overfitting and stabilize training.

nodes.title: Use TF-IDF features with n-grams up to 3
nodes.principle: Extract character n-grams (2-5) and word n-grams (1-3) using TF-IDF vectorization, limiting to 500-1000 features. Fit the vectorizer on the training fold only to prevent data leakage.
nodes.condition: When augmenting handcrafted features with n-gram signals for text classification.

nodes.title: Use TF-IDF n-gram features with character and word ranges
nodes.principle: Extract character n-grams (2-7), word n-grams (1-3), and punctuation sequences using TfidfVectorizer; optionally combine with handcrafted features for downstream classifiers.
nodes.condition: When building feature-based models for text classification, especially authorship attribution, to capture both style and content patterns.

nodes.title: Add gradient clipping to stabilize training and avoid NaN predictions
nodes.principle: Apply gradient clipping (e.g., max_norm=1.0) to prevent exploding gradients that cause NaN predictions.
nodes.condition: When training deep transformer models, especially with mixed precision.

nodes.title: Combine DeBERTa pooled embeddings with stylometric features for XGBoost meta-model
nodes.principle: Extract 15 stylometric features (avg word/sentence length, punctuation ratios, capitalization/digit ratios) and concatenate with DeBERTa pooled embeddings to train an XGBoost classifier, improving ensemble performance.
nodes.condition: When building an ensemble for authorship attribution tasks.

nodes.title: Define all functions and variables before use in script
nodes.principle: Ensure all custom functions (e.g., extract_stylometric_features) and variables are defined before they are called, and avoid forward references.
nodes.condition: When writing Python scripts to prevent NameError.

nodes.title: Use focal loss to handle class imbalance
nodes.principle: Use Focal Loss with gamma=1.5 and alpha=0.25 to focus on hard examples and mitigate class imbalance.
nodes.condition: When dealing with imbalanced classification tasks.

nodes.title: Use early stopping with patience based on validation loss to prevent overfitting
nodes.principle: Monitor validation loss after each epoch. Stop training if validation loss does not improve for a set number of epochs (patience). Restore model weights from the best epoch.
nodes.condition: When training neural networks and needing to prevent overfitting by stopping at the optimal point.

nodes.title: Use torch.load with weights_only=False for PyTorch 2.6+ compatibility
nodes.principle: When loading model state_dicts saved with older PyTorch versions, set weights_only=False in torch.load to avoid PicklingError due to restricted pickle modules.
nodes.condition: When loading PyTorch model checkpoints in PyTorch 2.6+ that were saved with model class context.

nodes.title: Ensure all model layers are on the correct device
nodes.principle: After creating custom layers (e.g., nn.Linear), explicitly move them to the target device using .to(device) or ensure they are created after the model is moved.
nodes.condition: When building custom model architectures with additional layers not part of the pretrained backbone.

nodes.title: Use focal loss with label smoothing to handle class imbalance and improve calibration
nodes.principle: Replace standard cross-entropy with focal loss (gamma=2, alpha=None) combined with label smoothing (epsilon=0.1). This reduces the loss contribution from well-classified examples and prevents overconfidence.
nodes.condition: When dealing with imbalanced classes or when the model produces overconfident predictions (e.g., validation log-loss plateaus).

nodes.title: Avoid progressive unfreezing that causes NaN losses due to optimizer re-initialization
nodes.principle: If using progressive unfreezing, do not recreate the optimizer mid-training. Instead, adjust learning rates for different parameter groups before training starts, or use a single learning rate for all layers.
nodes.condition: When fine-tuning transformers with layer-wise training; recreating optimizer can lead to instability and NaN losses.

nodes.title: Combine stylometric features with transformer embeddings for hybrid model
nodes.principle: Extract handcrafted stylometric features (punctuation density, sentence length, etc.) and concatenate with transformer pooled embeddings before classification.
nodes.condition: When performing authorship attribution or style-sensitive text classification.

nodes.title: Use multi-pooling head (CLS, mean, max, attention) with gated fusion
nodes.principle: Combine CLS, mean, max, and attention-weighted pooling via a learned gating mechanism to create a richer sentence representation.
nodes.condition: When using transformer models for text classification where pooling strategy matters.

nodes.title: Use TF-IDF features with n-grams up to 3 for text classification baseline
nodes.principle: Extract TF-IDF features with unigram, bigram, and trigram ranges (max 5000 features) as a strong baseline.
nodes.condition: When building a text classification pipeline.

nodes.title: Save model checkpoints based on validation log loss instead of cross-entropy loss
nodes.principle: Monitor and save the model checkpoint that achieves the lowest validation log loss (the competition metric), not the lowest cross-entropy loss, to directly optimize the target metric.
nodes.condition: When the evaluation metric is log loss and the model's cross-entropy loss does not correlate well with log loss.

nodes.title: Use two-phase training: freeze backbone then full fine-tuning with discriminative learning rates
nodes.principle: First train only the classifier head with the backbone frozen for a few epochs, then unfreeze the entire model and fine-tune with layer-wise learning rate decay (e.g., 1.0x for top layers, 0.95x per layer downward) to prevent overfitting.
nodes.condition: When fine-tuning a large transformer on a small dataset to avoid catastrophic forgetting.

nodes.title: Avoid passing unexpected keyword arguments to model forward methods
nodes.principle: When calling a custom model's forward method, ensure the method signature accepts all passed arguments; otherwise, modify the forward method to accept **kwargs or pass only expected arguments.
nodes.condition: When using custom model classes that override the forward method with a restricted signature.

nodes.title: Combine handcrafted stylometric features with transformer embeddings for hybrid model
nodes.principle: Extract handcrafted features (e.g., text length, punctuation ratios, readability scores, POS approximations) and concatenate them with transformer embeddings (e.g., mean-pooled DeBERTa embeddings). Train an XGBoost classifier on the combined feature set to capture both linguistic and stylistic patterns.
nodes.condition: When working on authorship attribution or style-based text classification tasks where handcrafted features complement transformer representations.

nodes.title: Use ConvNeXt-Tiny backbone with CutMix and MixUp for strong regularization
nodes.principle: Use a pretrained ConvNeXt-Tiny backbone from timm with a custom MLP classifier head. Apply CutMix (25% probability) and MixUp (25% probability) augmentations. Use AdamW optimizer with differential learning rates (backbone 5e-5, head 1e-3), warmup cosine annealing scheduler, label smoothing BCE loss, gradient clipping, and early stopping.
nodes.condition: When the current model (e.g., EfficientNet-B4) shows signs of overfitting (perfect validation AUC but compressed test predictions) and a stronger regularization approach is needed.

nodes.title: Avoid using RandAugment with magnitude parameter in older timm versions
nodes.principle: Use torchvision.transforms.TrivialAugmentWide instead of timm.data.RandAugment when the installed timm version does not support the magnitude parameter. Alternatively, omit the magnitude parameter and use default settings.
nodes.condition: When using RandAugment from timm and encountering TypeError about unexpected keyword argument 'magnitude', indicating an older timm version.

nodes.title: Ensure labels are float type for BCEWithLogitsLoss
nodes.principle: Convert target labels to float type (e.g., batch_y.float()) before passing to BCEWithLogitsLoss, as it expects float targets. Avoid using Long type which can cause type mismatch errors.
nodes.condition: When using BCEWithLogitsLoss and encountering 'result type Float can't be cast to the desired output type Long' error.

nodes.title: Use U-Net with Squeeze-and-Excitation blocks and combined MSE+SSIM loss for denoising
nodes.principle: Implement a U-Net autoencoder with Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) blocks in encoder/decoder, Gaussian noise injection, dropout, and skip connections. Train with a combined loss of MSE (or L1) and SSIM to improve perceptual quality and reduce RMSE.
nodes.condition: When denoising document images and the model plateaus with standard U-Net and MSE loss alone.

nodes.title: Use noise prior input channel (median filter residual) to improve denoising
nodes.principle: Compute a noise prior map as the residual between the noisy image and its median-filtered version, and stack it as an additional input channel (e.g., 2-channel input) to provide explicit noise information to the model.
nodes.condition: When denoising images with structured noise and the model benefits from explicit noise estimation.

nodes.title: Avoid creating new modules dynamically in forward pass to prevent device mismatch
nodes.principle: Define all layers (e.g., SEBlock) in __init__ and reuse them in forward; do not instantiate new modules inside forward to avoid CPU/GPU device mismatch.
nodes.condition: When building custom PyTorch models and encountering device mismatch errors during forward pass.

nodes.title: Use consistent image dimensions across all samples in a batch to avoid DataLoader collation errors
nodes.principle: Ensure all images in a batch have the same spatial dimensions by applying deterministic resizing or cropping after random augmentations, or by using a custom collate function that handles variable sizes.
nodes.condition: When using DataLoader with random augmentations that may change image dimensions (e.g., RandomAffine, RandomRotation).

nodes.title: Use multi-scale image feature extraction from SigLIP2 intermediate layers
nodes.principle: Extract image features from SigLIP2 by hooking into intermediate transformer layers (e.g., layers 12, 18, 24) and applying average pooling on patch tokens, then concatenating with the CLS token. This produces a richer feature representation (e.g., 4608-dim).
nodes.condition: When using SigLIP2 for leaf classification and needing richer image features beyond the final CLS token.

nodes.title: Avoid duplicate function definitions in the same script
nodes.principle: Ensure each function is defined only once in the script. Duplicate definitions can cause confusion and bugs due to the later definition overriding the earlier one.
nodes.condition: When writing or merging code from multiple sources.

nodes.title: Use correct function for softplus activation: F.softplus instead of torch.softplus
nodes.principle: Use torch.nn.functional.softplus (or F.softplus) for the softplus activation function, as torch.softplus does not exist.
nodes.condition: When implementing custom activation functions in PyTorch.

nodes.title: Avoid using torch.optim.swa_utils.update_bn with multi-input models
nodes.principle: When using Stochastic Weight Averaging (SWA) with models that take multiple inputs (e.g., separate feature groups), wrap the model to accept a single tuple or use a custom BN update loop, as update_bn expects a single input tensor.
nodes.condition: When applying SWA to models with multiple forward arguments.

nodes.title: Fit scaler on training data only to prevent data leakage
nodes.principle: Fit StandardScaler (or any scaler) only on the training set, then transform both training and validation sets separately, to avoid leaking validation statistics.
nodes.condition: When normalizing features using a scaler that computes statistics from the data.

nodes.title: Use single-stage LightGBM with proper categorical handling for taxi fare prediction
nodes.principle: Train a single-stage LightGBM regressor with high leaf count (127), max depth 15, learning rate 0.02, and early stopping, ensuring categorical features are passed as indices and not scaled.
nodes.condition: When building a strong baseline for NYC taxi fare prediction with large dataset.

nodes.title: Use temporal train/validation split to avoid data leakage
nodes.principle: Split the data chronologically based on pickup datetime (e.g., 80% earliest for training, 20% latest for validation) to respect the time series nature of taxi trips.
nodes.condition: When dealing with time-ordered data like taxi trips where future information should not leak into training.

nodes.title: Avoid two-stage residual boosting for taxi fare prediction
nodes.principle: Single-stage LightGBM with proper regularization outperforms two-stage residual boosting, which provides negligible improvement and risks overfitting.
nodes.condition: When designing the modeling approach for NYC taxi fare prediction.

nodes.title: Use smaller model variant to avoid CUDA OOM
nodes.principle: When encountering CUDA out-of-memory errors, switch to a smaller model variant (e.g., DeBERTa-v3-small or ModernBERT-base instead of DeBERTa-v3-large or ModernBERT-large) and reduce batch size (e.g., batch_size=8), max sequence length (e.g., max_length=256), and gradient accumulation steps to fit GPU memory.
nodes.condition: When GPU memory is insufficient for a large transformer model, causing CUDA OOM errors during training.

nodes.title: Match model input dimension to actual feature dimension
nodes.principle: Ensure the model's input dimension exactly matches the concatenated feature vector dimension. Compute the actual dimension after all feature extraction steps and set input_dim accordingly.
nodes.condition: When building a model that takes concatenated features from multiple sources (e.g., SBERT + TF-IDF + stylometric).

nodes.title: Define all variables before use in script
nodes.principle: Ensure all variables are defined before they are referenced, especially when using functions that return multiple values. Assign returned vectorizers, embeddings, etc. to named variables in the correct order.
nodes.condition: When writing a long script with multiple feature extraction steps and function calls.

nodes.title: Use progressive unfreezing with linear decay and single optimizer to prevent overfitting
nodes.principle: Start with only the classifier head trainable, then gradually unfreeze encoder layers (e.g., last 4 layers after epoch 2, next 4 after epoch 3) without recreating the optimizer; use a single AdamW optimizer with differential learning rates (classifier LR = backbone LR * 5-10).
nodes.condition: When fine-tuning a large transformer (ModernBERT, RoBERTa, etc.) on a small dataset to avoid catastrophic overfitting.

nodes.title: Use gradient clipping to stabilize training
nodes.principle: Clip gradient norm to a maximum value (e.g., 1.0) after unscaling (if using AMP) and before optimizer step to prevent exploding gradients.
nodes.condition: When training deep networks, especially transformers, to avoid training instability or gradient explosion.

nodes.title: Use 5-fold cross-validation with DistilBERT and CrossEntropyLoss for improved generalization
nodes.principle: Use 5-fold StratifiedKFold cross-validation with DistilBERT, CrossEntropyLoss, AdamW optimizer, cosine schedule with warmup, gradient accumulation (2 steps), gradient clipping, mixed precision, and early stopping. Average test predictions across folds.
nodes.condition: When aiming to reduce overfitting and improve generalization in Spooky Author Identification with a transformer model.

nodes.title: Use DistilRoBERTa with BiLSTM and Focal Loss for style modeling
nodes.principle: Use DistilRoBERTa-base encoder with mean pooling over all token embeddings, followed by a 2-layer bidirectional LSTM (hidden_dim=256) with residual connection and layer normalization, then a linear classifier. Train with Focal Loss (gamma=2.0), AdamW optimizer, linear warmup scheduler, gradient accumulation (4 steps), mixed precision, and early stopping.
nodes.condition: When wanting to capture sequential style patterns and improve generalization over a simple CLS head for Spooky Author Identification.

nodes.title: Import AdamW from torch.optim instead of transformers
nodes.principle: Use `from torch.optim import AdamW` instead of `from transformers import AdamW` because the latter is deprecated in newer versions of the transformers library and may raise an ImportError.
nodes.condition: When using AdamW optimizer in a PyTorch training script with the transformers library.

nodes.title: Use float16-representable negative value in masked_fill
nodes.principle: When using masked_fill with a large negative value (e.g., -1e9) in float16 (e.g., under AMP), use a value representable in float16 such as -1e4 or torch.finfo(torch.float16).min to prevent overflow errors.
nodes.condition: When implementing attention pooling or similar operations with masked_fill under mixed precision training (float16), especially in transformer models with AMP.

nodes.title: Avoid passing dropout params directly to from_pretrained
nodes.principle: Do not pass 'hidden_dropout_prob' or 'attention_probs_dropout_prob' as keyword arguments to from_pretrained(). Instead, modify the model's configuration after loading or use a config object. Passing these directly causes a TypeError.
nodes.condition: When loading a pretrained model (e.g., DeBERTa, ModernBERT) from HuggingFace transformers and needing to adjust dropout rates.

nodes.title: Ensure model input dimensions match actual hidden size
nodes.principle: When concatenating transformer embeddings with engineered features, verify the transformer's hidden size (e.g., ModernBERT-large has hidden_size=1024, not 768). The classifier input dimension must be hidden_size + feature_dim.
nodes.condition: When building a hybrid model that combines transformer outputs with additional features.

nodes.title: Avoid passing label_smoothing_factor to Hugging Face from_pretrained
nodes.principle: Do not pass label_smoothing_factor as a keyword argument to AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained(); instead, apply label smoothing via the loss function (e.g., CrossEntropyLoss with label_smoothing).
nodes.condition: When using Hugging Face transformers and attempting to add label smoothing.

nodes.title: Use progressive unfreezing with warm-up and differential learning rates to improve generalization
nodes.principle: Train transformer models in phases: first freeze backbone and train only the head for a few epochs, then gradually unfreeze layers with lower learning rates (e.g., 1e-6 for backbone, 2e-5 for head) and use a warm-up phase to stabilize training.
nodes.condition: When fine-tuning a large transformer model to prevent overfitting and improve validation loss.

nodes.title: Use two-phase training with different stratified splits to improve performance
nodes.principle: Train in two phases: Phase 1 on a stratified split (e.g., 17k train / 500 val) with warm-up and differential learning rates, then Phase 2 on a different stratified split to leverage more data and reduce overfitting.
nodes.condition: When aiming for best performance on a small dataset with a transformer model.

nodes.title: Use TextCNN with random embeddings and stylometric features for text classification
nodes.principle: Tokenize text, build vocabulary, use trainable random embeddings (128-dim) with Xavier initialization, apply multi-filter CNN (kernel sizes 2,3,4,5, 128 filters each) with batch norm, ReLU, global max pooling, dropout (0.3), combine with 6 stylometric features via MLP branch, train with label smoothing cross-entropy, AdamW, and early stopping.
nodes.condition: When transformer models are unavailable or too slow, and a CNN-based approach is preferred for text classification.

nodes.title: Avoid NaN predictions by simplifying attention mechanisms and using gradient clipping
nodes.principle: When using complex attention pooling (e.g., weighted layer attention, multi-head attention) with mixed precision, simplify architecture or add gradient clipping (norm=1.0) and torch.nan_to_num to prevent NaN outputs.
nodes.condition: When training transformer models with custom attention layers and mixed precision, to avoid numerical instability.

nodes.title: Use correct indexing for StratifiedKFold splits
nodes.principle: When using StratifiedKFold, ensure that the indices from split() are applied to the full dataset, not to a subset that has already been reduced in size, to avoid IndexError.
nodes.condition: When performing cross-validation with StratifiedKFold on a dataset that has been pre-filtered or partially indexed.

nodes.title: Clip probabilities after softmax to avoid NaN in log_loss
nodes.principle: After computing softmax probabilities, clip them to a small epsilon range (e.g., 1e-7, 1-1e-7) to avoid log(0) and NaN values when computing log loss.
