nodes.condition: When computing cross-entropy or log loss on model outputs, especially with numerical instability.

nodes.title: Use consistent variable names to avoid NameError
nodes.principle: Ensure that variable names used in code are defined and spelled consistently. Avoid referencing undefined variables or using different suffixes (e.g., test_features vs test_features_fold).
nodes.condition: When writing Python scripts with multiple variables.

nodes.title: Use ensemble of DeBERTa-v3-large, XGBoost, and Logistic Regression with weight optimization
nodes.principle: Combine predictions from fine-tuned DeBERTa-v3-large (with label smoothing, early stopping, mixed precision), XGBoost trained on DeBERTa embeddings plus handcrafted features, and Logistic Regression on TF-IDF n-gram features. Optimize ensemble weights via grid search on validation log loss.
nodes.condition: When tackling text classification tasks with limited data where transformer overfitting is a concern, and maximum performance is needed with computational resources for multiple models.

nodes.title: Avoid using torch.no_grad() inside autocast() when gradients are needed
nodes.principle: Do not wrap operations that require gradients with torch.no_grad() inside an autocast context. If MixUp or similar augmentation requires no_grad, compute it outside the training loop or on logits after forward pass.
nodes.condition: When implementing data augmentation that mixes samples (e.g., MixUp) and using mixed precision training.

nodes.title: Ensure classifier input dimension matches actual concatenated feature dimension
nodes.principle: When building multi-encoder models, compute the total feature dimension by running a dummy forward pass or carefully summing encoder output dimensions. Verify that the classifier's first linear layer input size matches the actual concatenated feature size.
nodes.condition: When building multi-encoder neural networks with concatenated features.

nodes.title: Avoid data augmentation that creates size mismatch between features and labels
nodes.principle: When applying back-translation or other augmentation, ensure that the number of augmented samples matches the number of labels. Duplicate labels accordingly or use a dataset that handles augmentation internally.
nodes.condition: When augmenting text data; mismatched sizes cause TensorDataset creation errors.

nodes.title: Verify each sub-goal succeeds before proceeding in multi-stage pipelines
nodes.principle: After each stage (feature extraction, model training, checkpoint saving, embedding extraction), print confirmation or check outputs. Ensure no silent failures before moving to next stage.
nodes.condition: When building complex multi-stage pipelines; early detection of bugs prevents wasted compute.

nodes.title: Use correct attribute name for ModernBERT embedding layer
nodes.principle: Access ModernBERT's embedding layer via model.model.embeddings.tok_embeddings, not word_embeddings.
nodes.condition: When implementing mixup or other techniques that require direct access to the embedding layer of ModernBERT.

nodes.title: Move loss function weights to same device as input tensors
nodes.principle: Ensure all buffers in custom loss functions (e.g., AdaptiveFocalLoss.weights) are moved to the same device as the input tensors.
nodes.condition: When implementing custom loss functions that use per-class weights.

nodes.title: Use multi-layer pooling (weighted average of last hidden layers) for transformer embeddings
nodes.principle: Instead of using only the CLS token, compute a weighted average of the last 3-4 hidden layers' token embeddings, then apply mean pooling over tokens to obtain a richer sentence representation.
nodes.condition: When the CLS token alone does not capture sufficient contextual information for downstream tasks.

nodes.title: Ensure model checkpoint architecture matches when saving and loading
nodes.principle: When saving a model checkpoint, save only the state_dict and ensure the model architecture used for loading is exactly the same as during saving, including any custom heads or feature fusion layers.
nodes.condition: When using custom model architectures or when loading a checkpoint into a different model instance.

nodes.title: Use 5-fold stratified cross-validation with OOF predictions for robust ensemble
nodes.principle: Implement 5-fold stratified cross-validation to generate out-of-fold (OOF) predictions from each model, then train a meta-learner (e.g., logistic regression) on OOF probabilities to learn ensemble weights. This reduces overfitting and improves generalization compared to a single train/validation split.
nodes.condition: When building an ensemble of multiple models (e.g., transformer, XGBoost, logistic regression) for classification, and the dataset is small enough to allow multiple training runs.

nodes.title: Use ensemble of EfficientNet-B0 and ResNet-18 with spatial attention for improved robustness
nodes.principle: Create an ensemble of EfficientNet-B0 and ResNet-18 models, each with a spatial attention module. Use 5-fold stratified cross-validation, RandAugment and CutMix augmentations, BCEWithLogitsLoss, AdamW optimizer with warmup and cosine annealing scheduler. Average predictions from all folds and both models for final submission.
nodes.condition: When wanting to improve robustness and generalization beyond a single model for aerial cactus identification.

nodes.title: Set DataLoader num_workers=0 to avoid shared memory issues in containerized environments
nodes.principle: Set num_workers=0 and pin_memory=False in DataLoader to avoid shared memory (shm) exhaustion, which causes bus errors and worker crashes. This trades off data loading speed for reliability.
nodes.condition: When running in environments with limited shared memory (e.g., Docker containers, Kaggle notebooks) and experiencing DataLoader worker crashes due to shm issues.

nodes.title: Avoid computing train AUC when mixup augmentation produces continuous labels
nodes.principle: Skip computing training AUC when mixup augmentation is applied, as the continuous labels (floats between 0 and 1) are incompatible with roc_auc_score which expects binary labels. Only compute validation AUC on non-mixed batches.
nodes.condition: When using mixup augmentation during training and attempting to compute training AUC with sklearn's roc_auc_score.

nodes.title: Use correct indexing for EfficientNet backbone blocks when unfreezing
nodes.principle: When unfreezing specific blocks of an EfficientNet backbone from timm, iterate over the blocks list and unfreeze the last N blocks by index (e.g., for EfficientNet-B0, blocks are indexed 0-6, so unfreeze blocks[4:] for last 3 blocks). Use len(backbone.blocks) to determine the total number of blocks.
nodes.condition: When implementing partial fine-tuning of EfficientNet models from timm and needing to unfreeze specific blocks by index.

nodes.title: Add gradient clipping and input validation to prevent NaN predictions
nodes.principle: Use gradient clipping (max_norm=1.0) and add input validation (e.g., clamp inputs to valid range) to prevent NaN values in model outputs. Also ensure mixed precision training uses consistent autocast context and proper GradScaler usage.
nodes.condition: When model produces NaN predictions during training or validation, often due to numerical instability or exploding gradients.

nodes.title: Use DINOv2 ViT-S/14 encoder with trainable backbone and differential learning rates
nodes.principle: Use a pretrained DINOv2 ViT-S/14 as encoder, with a small warmup LR for the backbone (e.g., linear warmup from 0 to 5e-5) and a higher LR for the decoder (e.g., 1e-3), and unfreeze the last few encoder blocks after warmup.
nodes.condition: When using a vision transformer backbone for image denoising and the frozen encoder limits adaptation to the task.

nodes.title: Avoid using IPython magic commands (!pip) in standard Python scripts
nodes.principle: Do not use Jupyter/IPython magic commands like '!pip install' in standard Python scripts. Use subprocess calls or ensure dependencies are pre-installed.
nodes.condition: When writing Python scripts for execution outside of Jupyter notebooks.

nodes.title: Define all functions before their first use in the script
nodes.principle: Place all function definitions at the top of the script, before any code that calls them, to avoid NameError due to Python's top-to-bottom execution order.
nodes.condition: When writing Python scripts with custom functions.

nodes.title: Use per-group PCA and separate scaling for structured tabular features
nodes.principle: Split features into groups (e.g., margin, shape, texture), apply StandardScaler and PCA (retaining 95% variance) independently per group to preserve group-specific structure and reduce dimensionality without mixing information.
nodes.condition: When dealing with tabular data that has natural feature groupings (e.g., leaf margin/shape/texture) and a small sample size relative to feature dimension.

nodes.title: Use multi-branch MLP with per-group branches and cross-attention fusion
nodes.principle: Design a neural network with separate MLP branches for each feature group (e.g., margin, shape, texture), then fuse via cross-attention mechanism followed by a classifier head. Use moderate dropout (0.3) and batch normalization.
nodes.condition: When tabular features have natural groupings and a multi-branch architecture can capture inter-group interactions.

nodes.title: Avoid passing verbose_eval as keyword argument to lgb.train
nodes.principle: Use the 'verbose' parameter in the model params dict or lgb.log_evaluation callback instead of passing verbose_eval as a keyword argument to lgb.train.
nodes.condition: When using LightGBM's train function and wanting to control logging verbosity.

nodes.title: Use DeBERTa-v3-base with partial freezing and label smoothing
nodes.principle: Fine-tune DeBERTa-v3-base with the first 8 layers frozen, label smoothing (0.1), gradient clipping, mixed precision, and early stopping. Use a single 90/10 stratified split for more epochs.
nodes.condition: When fine-tuning a medium-sized transformer for text classification with limited data.

nodes.title: Define variables before use in training scripts
nodes.principle: Ensure all variables (e.g., train_loader, num_epochs) are defined before they are referenced, especially when setting up schedulers or computing total steps.
nodes.condition: When writing training loops that depend on DataLoaders or epoch counts.

nodes.title: Use AdamW from torch.optim instead of transformers
nodes.principle: Import AdamW from torch.optim (from torch.optim import AdamW) rather than from transformers to avoid ImportError due to version incompatibility in newer versions of transformers.
nodes.condition: When using AdamW optimizer in a training script or with HuggingFace transformers.

nodes.title: Use 5-fold cross-validation with MiniLM transformer and sparse features
nodes.principle: Train a MiniLM transformer fused with sparse TF-IDF and stylistic features using 5-fold cross-validation, averaging predictions across folds for better generalization.
nodes.condition: When aiming for robust performance on a small text classification dataset.

nodes.title: Use word-level perturbation augmentation (random swap/delete) instead of synonym replacement
nodes.principle: Apply mild word-level augmentation: random token swap (probability 0.1) and random token deletion (probability 0.1) to training texts. This regularizes without distorting authorial style.
nodes.condition: When augmenting text data for authorship attribution; avoid synonym replacement which can alter author voice.

nodes.title: Access ModernBERT backbone via model.model attribute
nodes.principle: For ModernBertForSequenceClassification, the underlying encoder is accessed via model.model (not model.bert or model.modern_bert). In a custom subclass, use self.model.encoder.layer for layer-wise operations.
nodes.condition: When implementing custom forward passes, progressive unfreezing, or creating a custom model that wraps ModernBertForSequenceClassification.

nodes.title: Use stylometric features (hand-crafted text statistics) as additional input to transformer
nodes.principle: Extract features like character/word counts, punctuation frequencies, readability scores, archaic word indicators, and n-gram densities; scale them and concatenate with transformer [CLS] embedding via a small MLP encoder before classification.
nodes.condition: When performing authorship attribution to capture stylistic patterns not fully captured by transformers.

nodes.title: Use DistilRoBERTa with multi-head attention pooling and SWA for improved performance
nodes.principle: Use DistilRoBERTa-base with multi-head attention pooling (8 heads) to aggregate token embeddings, plus a residual mean-pooled connection and a linear classifier. Train with Focal Loss (gamma=2.0), AdamW optimizer, linear warmup scheduler, gradient accumulation (4 steps), mixed precision, and apply Stochastic Weight Averaging (SWA) averaging top 3 checkpoints.
nodes.condition: When wanting to improve performance over mean pooling for Spooky Author Identification; attention pooling can better capture important tokens.

nodes.title: Ensure model forward method returns logits as a tensor or as an object with .logits attribute consistently
nodes.principle: When using a custom model (not HuggingFace AutoModel), ensure the forward method returns logits in a format consistent with the training loop. If the training loop expects `outputs.logits`, the model should return an object with a `.logits` attribute; if it expects a plain tensor, the model should return a tensor directly.
nodes.condition: When mixing custom model implementations with training loops designed for HuggingFace models.

nodes.title: Use CalibratedClassifierCV with estimator parameter in newer scikit-learn
nodes.principle: When using CalibratedClassifierCV from scikit-learn >=1.0, use the parameter name 'estimator' instead of 'base_estimator' or 'base_engine'.
nodes.condition: When calibrating a classifier with CalibratedClassifierCV in scikit-learn version 1.0 or later.

nodes.title: Move all tensors to the same device in custom forward methods
nodes.principle: When using custom model forward methods that combine multiple inputs (e.g., transformer outputs and feature tensors), ensure all tensors are moved to the same device (e.g., via .to(device) or by passing device argument).
nodes.condition: When implementing custom PyTorch models that process multiple input tensors and using GPU training.

nodes.title: Use 5-fold cross-validation with ensemble averaging to improve generalization
nodes.principle: Train separate models on each fold of a 5-fold stratified split and average their predictions (or use a meta-model) to reduce variance and improve test performance.
nodes.condition: When aiming for robust performance on a classification task with limited data.

nodes.title: Use synonym replacement augmentation via WordNet to reduce overfitting
nodes.principle: Apply synonym replacement to training texts using WordNet to augment the dataset and improve generalization.
nodes.condition: When training a text classification model and overfitting is observed.

nodes.title: Use two-phase training with frozen backbone then full fine-tuning with proper device handling
nodes.principle: When fine-tuning a transformer model, first train with frozen backbone for a few epochs, then unfreeze all parameters and continue training with a lower learning rate. Ensure all tensors are on the same device and use gradient clipping to avoid CUDA errors.
nodes.condition: When fine-tuning large transformer models on a GPU to prevent overfitting and CUDA memory issues.

nodes.title: Use CPU tensors for model checkpoint saving to avoid file write errors
nodes.principle: When saving model checkpoints, move tensors to CPU first (model.to('cpu')) to avoid file write errors that can occur with GPU tensors in multi-worker settings.
nodes.condition: When saving PyTorch model checkpoints in environments with limited disk space or concurrent writes.

nodes.title: Avoid duplicate parameter groups in optimizer
nodes.principle: Ensure that no parameter appears in more than one parameter group when creating the optimizer, by using set operations or careful grouping, to avoid ValueError.
nodes.condition: When using differential learning rates or layer-wise parameter groups with AdamW.

nodes.title: Ensure model state_dict keys match when loading checkpoint
nodes.principle: When saving and loading a custom model, ensure the architecture is identical at save and load time, or use strict=False and handle missing/unexpected keys appropriately.
nodes.condition: When fine-tuning a custom transformer model and reloading the best checkpoint for inference or ensemble.

nodes.title: Use stratified index-based split to avoid data leakage
nodes.principle: Use StratifiedKFold or train_test_split with stratify=y and random_state to generate indices, then split dataframes using .iloc or numpy indexing, ensuring no overlap between train and validation sets.
nodes.condition: When performing cross-validation or a single train/validation split for classification tasks with imbalanced classes to prevent accidental data leakage.

nodes.title: Use cosine annealing scheduler with warmup for transformer fine-tuning
nodes.principle: Use torch.optim.lr_scheduler.CosineAnnealingLR or OneCycleLR with linear warmup to gradually decrease learning rate, improving convergence.
nodes.condition: When fine-tuning transformer models for classification tasks.

nodes.title: Remove merge conflict markers and extraneous text from code
nodes.principle: Before executing code, remove any merge conflict markers (<<<<<<<, =======, >>>>>>>) and any natural language instructions or markdown artifacts embedded in the code.
nodes.condition: When preparing code for execution to avoid syntax errors.

nodes.title: Use consistent tensor dimensions in pooling operations
nodes.principle: When applying pooling (mean, max) to LSTM or transformer outputs, ensure the mask tensor has the same sequence length as the actual output tensor after packing/unpacking. Use the original mask on the embedded input rather than on the packed/unpacked output.
nodes.condition: When implementing custom pooling on variable-length sequences with masking.

nodes.title: Ensure EMA shadow dictionary is updated when adding new parameters
nodes.principle: After progressive unfreezing adds new trainable parameters, re-register EMA to include the new parameters in the shadow dictionary.
nodes.condition: When using EMA with progressive unfreezing that adds new trainable parameters mid-training.

nodes.title: Define all variables and DataLoaders before they are used in the script
nodes.principle: Ensure that every variable, DataLoader, and function is defined earlier in the script than its first usage, especially in multi-stage pipelines where later stages depend on earlier ones.
nodes.condition: When writing long scripts with multiple sequential stages to avoid NameError at runtime.

nodes.title: Use penalty=None instead of penalty='none' in scikit-learn LogisticRegression
nodes.principle: When initializing LogisticRegression with no penalty, set penalty=None (Python None), not the string 'none'. The string 'none' is invalid and causes an InvalidParameterError.
nodes.condition: When using scikit-learn's LogisticRegression with penalty=None.

nodes.title: Use EfficientNet-B3 with progressive resizing for improved generalization
nodes.principle: Use a pretrained EfficientNet-B3 backbone with progressive resizing (start at 160px, then 192px, then 224px) with corresponding batch sizes (64, 48, 32). Train with BCEWithLogitsLoss, AdamW optimizer, linear warmup for 3 epochs followed by cosine annealing, CutMix augmentation, and early stopping. Use test-time augmentation (horizontal flip averaging) for final predictions.
nodes.condition: When aiming for near-perfect validation AUC (>0.9999) on aerial cactus identification and wanting to reduce overfitting through curriculum learning on image resolution.

nodes.title: Use EfficientNet-B4 with CBAM attention and MixUp/CutMix for best performance
nodes.principle: Use a pretrained EfficientNet-B4 backbone with a custom CBAM attention head and 3-layer MLP classifier. Apply RandAugment, RandomErasing, MixUp (80% probability), and CutMix (25% probability) augmentations. Train with Focal Loss with label smoothing, AdamW optimizer, OneCycleLR scheduler, mixed precision, and early stopping. Use test-time augmentation (horizontal flip) for final predictions.
nodes.condition: When aiming for the highest possible validation AUC (1.0) on aerial cactus identification and computational resources allow for a larger model.

nodes.title: Avoid passing label_smoothing parameter to BCEWithLogitsLoss in older PyTorch versions
nodes.principle: Check PyTorch version before using label_smoothing with BCEWithLogitsLoss. If version < 1.10, implement label smoothing manually or use standard BCEWithLogitsLoss without label_smoothing.
nodes.condition: When using BCEWithLogitsLoss with label smoothing in environments where PyTorch version may be older than 1.10 (label_smoothing parameter introduced in PyTorch 1.10).

nodes.title: Use correct attribute path for HuggingFace model backbone layers
nodes.principle: Access backbone layers via the correct attribute name (e.g., model.backbone for ModernBERT, model.dinov2 for DINOv2) to avoid AttributeError when building custom heads.
nodes.condition: When using HuggingFace transformer models and accessing internal layers for feature extraction.

nodes.title: Ensure DataLoader objects are defined before use in training loops
nodes.principle: After feature engineering and dataset creation, explicitly create DataLoader objects (train_loader, val_loader, etc.) before entering the training loop. Verify all loader variables are defined.
nodes.condition: When implementing a PyTorch training pipeline with separate data loaders.

nodes.title: Use XGBoost with hist tree method for CPU compatibility
nodes.principle: Set XGBoost tree_method='hist' instead of 'gpu_hist' to avoid GPU compatibility issues, and move early_stopping_rounds to the constructor for older XGBoost versions.
nodes.condition: When using XGBoost and encountering 'gpu_hist not supported' or 'early_stopping_rounds' parameter errors.

nodes.title: Use two-stage fine-tuning with frozen backbone then full fine-tuning
nodes.principle: First train only the classifier head and gating network with frozen backbone for a few epochs, then unfreeze all layers for full fine-tuning. This prevents overfitting and improves generalization.
nodes.condition: When fine-tuning a transformer on a small dataset to avoid overfitting.

nodes.title: Use multi-layer CLS aggregation with learned gating
nodes.principle: Aggregate [CLS] tokens from multiple transformer layers (e.g., last 3 or all 6) using a learnable gating mechanism to combine layer representations, improving feature richness.
nodes.condition: When using a transformer backbone for classification and wanting to leverage intermediate representations.

nodes.title: Use attention pooling for sentence representation
nodes.principle: Replace [CLS] token with a learned attention pooling layer: compute attention scores over all token embeddings via a learned query vector, apply softmax, and produce a weighted sum of token embeddings.
nodes.condition: When using transformer models for classification and needing a more expressive sentence embedding than [CLS].

nodes.title: Use DistilBERT with 3-fold cross-validation and early stopping for moderate performance
nodes.principle: Use DistilBertForSequenceClassification with max_length=128, 3-fold stratified cross-validation, AdamW optimizer (from torch.optim), cosine LR scheduler with warmup, gradient clipping, and early stopping (patience=2). Average predictions across folds, clip and normalize probabilities. This balances performance and training time.
nodes.condition: When a transformer model is needed but computational resources are limited and overfitting is a concern.

nodes.title: Use DeBERTa-v3-base with 3-fold cross-validation and early stopping for strong performance
nodes.principle: Use AutoModelForSequenceClassification with 'microsoft/deberta-v3-base', max_length=256, 3-fold stratified cross-validation, AdamW optimizer, cosine scheduler with warmup, CrossEntropyLoss, and early stopping (patience=2). Average predictions across folds, clip and normalize. This achieves log-loss around 0.38 on the spooky-author-identification task.
nodes.condition: When aiming for strong performance on text classification with moderate dataset size and computational budget.

nodes.title: Avoid merge conflict markers in code files
nodes.principle: Remove any merge conflict markers (e.g., '=======', '>>>>>>>') from the code before execution to prevent SyntaxError.
nodes.condition: When editing code files that may contain version control conflict artifacts.

nodes.title: Use Exponential Moving Average (EMA) for model weights
nodes.principle: Maintain an exponential moving average of model parameters during training and use the EMA model for validation and inference to improve generalization.
nodes.condition: When training deep neural networks to stabilize training and improve performance.

nodes.title: Use progressive unfreezing with warm-up and differential learning rates
nodes.principle: Gradually unfreeze transformer layers from top to bottom with different learning rates (higher for later layers) and a warm-up phase.
nodes.condition: When fine-tuning large pre-trained models to prevent catastrophic forgetting and improve convergence.

nodes.title: Use mean pooling of transformer hidden states instead of CLS token for better sentence representation
nodes.principle: Apply mean pooling over all token hidden states from the last transformer layer (or last two layers) to obtain a fixed-size sentence embedding. Use this embedding as input to a classifier head.
nodes.condition: When using a transformer model for text classification and CLS token representation is suboptimal.

nodes.title: Use AdamW optimizer with weight decay for transformer fine-tuning
nodes.principle: Use AdamW from torch.optim with weight decay (e.g., 0.01) and separate parameter groups for bias and LayerNorm terms (no decay).
nodes.condition: When fine-tuning transformer models and needing proper weight decay regularization.

nodes.title: Avoid using DataLoader methods like .skip() and .take()
nodes.principle: DataLoader objects do not have .skip() or .take() methods. To iterate over multiple DataLoaders simultaneously, use zip() or enumerate with indices.
nodes.condition: When iterating over DataLoaders and needing to access specific batches.

nodes.title: Use LightGBM meta-classifier on transformer embeddings and handcrafted features
nodes.principle: After training a transformer (e.g., RoBERTa, DeBERTa), extract pooled embeddings from the best checkpoint. Concatenate with handcrafted features (stylometric, readability, POS, n-gram TF-IDF). Train a LightGBM classifier on the combined features using the validation set. Use the LightGBM predictions as a meta-learner to improve ensemble performance.
nodes.condition: When transformer fine-tuning yields moderate validation log-loss (e.g., 0.44) and additional feature engineering is available; LightGBM can capture non-linear interactions.

nodes.title: Avoid FGM adversarial training with torch.compile or retain_graph=True
nodes.principle: Remove FGM adversarial training or ensure backward passes do not use retain_graph=True when using torch.compile.
nodes.condition: When using ModernBERT with torch.compile and adversarial training.

nodes.title: Use AdaptiveFocalLoss with label smoothing for imbalanced classification
nodes.principle: Use focal loss with adaptive gamma and label smoothing to handle class imbalance and improve calibration.
nodes.condition: When dealing with imbalanced text classification tasks.

nodes.title: Use temporal ensemble of top-K checkpoints for transformer predictions
nodes.principle: After fine-tuning, average the predicted probabilities from the top-K checkpoints (e.g., top 3 by validation log loss) using inverse log-loss weighting to stabilize predictions and improve calibration.
nodes.condition: When fine-tuning a transformer model and the best single checkpoint shows high variance or overfitting.

nodes.title: Define all variables and functions before use in training scripts
nodes.principle: Ensure all variables, functions, and classes are defined before they are referenced in the code. This includes DataLoaders, datasets, model instances, and utility functions like cutmix.
nodes.condition: When writing training scripts to avoid NameError caused by referencing undefined variables or functions.

nodes.title: Use SigLIP2 vision transformer with two-stage fine-tuning for leaf classification
nodes.principle: Use SigLIP2 (google/siglip2-so400m-patch16-256) as image feature extractor. In Stage 1, freeze SigLIP2 and train only an MLP classifier head. In Stage 2, fine-tune the last 2 transformer blocks of SigLIP2 along with the head using a lower learning rate. Use differential learning rates, label smoothing, and early stopping.
nodes.condition: When using SigLIP2 for leaf classification and the frozen encoder plateaus; to improve feature adaptation to the target dataset.

nodes.title: Access transformer backbone attributes correctly
nodes.principle: When freezing or accessing transformer backbone parameters, use the correct attribute name (e.g., model.bert for BERT, model.model for ModernBERT). Check the model's source or documentation.
nodes.condition: When working with HuggingFace transformer models and needing to access internal layers.

nodes.title: Use ensemble of DistilBERT, XGBoost on TF-IDF, and CharCNN-LSTM
nodes.principle: Combine predictions from a fine-tuned DistilBERT, an XGBoost model trained on TF-IDF + stylistic features, and a character-level CNN-LSTM, weighted by validation performance. This ensemble breaks plateaus.
nodes.condition: When a single model's validation log-loss plateaus and additional diversity is needed.

nodes.title: Combine multiple frozen transformer embeddings with XGBoost stacking
nodes.principle: Extract embeddings from several pretrained transformers (e.g., RoBERTa, DeBERTa, ALBERT) using mean pooling, then train an XGBoost classifier on the concatenated embeddings with probability outputs from base models as additional features.
nodes.condition: When aiming for best performance on text classification with limited compute; ensemble of diverse transformers improves generalization.

nodes.title: Avoid gradient checkpointing conflict with GradScaler
nodes.principle: Do not use gradient_checkpointing_enable() together with torch.cuda.amp.GradScaler, as it causes 'Trying to backward through the graph a second time' error. Either disable checkpointing or restructure backward pass.
nodes.condition: When using mixed precision training with gradient checkpointing.

nodes.title: Use multi-sample dropout for improved generalization
nodes.principle: Apply K forward passes with different dropout masks (K=4) and average the logits during training to regularize the model.
nodes.condition: When fine-tuning transformer models to reduce overfitting on small datasets.

nodes.title: Use mixed precision training with GradScaler for memory efficiency and speed
nodes.principle: Use torch.cuda.amp.autocast and GradScaler to enable mixed precision training. Scale loss before backward and unscale gradients before clipping.
nodes.condition: When training large models on GPU and wanting to reduce memory usage and speed up training.

nodes.title: Ensure OOF prediction arrays have consistent shapes across folds
nodes.principle: When assembling out-of-fold predictions, ensure each fold's validation predictions are placed at the correct indices in a pre-allocated array of shape (n_samples, n_classes). Do not stack arrays of different sizes.
nodes.condition: When implementing cross-validation and collecting out-of-fold predictions.

nodes.title: Use DeBERTa-v3-base with mean pooling and simple MLP classifier for stable fine-tuning
nodes.principle: Load DeBERTa-v3-base with AutoModel (not AutoModelForSequenceClassification). Apply mean pooling over token embeddings (excluding padding). Add a 2-layer MLP classifier (e.g., hidden size 256) with dropout. Train with cross-entropy loss (label smoothing 0.1), AdamW (lr 2e-5), cosine scheduler with warmup, gradient accumulation (4 steps), and mixed precision. Use early stopping on validation log-loss.
nodes.condition: When a moderate-sized transformer is needed to avoid CUDA OOM while still achieving good performance on text classification.

nodes.title: Use smaller model variant (DeBERTa-v3-base) to avoid CUDA OOM when compute is limited
nodes.principle: If DeBERTa-v3-large causes out-of-memory errors or timeouts, switch to DeBERTa-v3-base with similar training setup (mean pooling, label smoothing, gradient accumulation).
nodes.condition: When GPU memory is insufficient for large transformer models; base model still achieves competitive performance.

nodes.title: Initialize optimizer before training loop to avoid NameError
nodes.principle: Define the optimizer outside the epoch loop, ensuring it is always available even when no stage transition occurs.
nodes.condition: When using progressive unfreezing with stage-dependent optimizer creation.

nodes.title: Use progressive unfreezing with EMA and FGM for stable fine-tuning
nodes.principle: Freeze backbone initially, then progressively unfreeze layers while using EMA and FGM adversarial training to stabilize training and improve generalization.
nodes.condition: When fine-tuning large transformers on small datasets to avoid overfitting.

nodes.title: Apply temperature scaling to calibrate transformer probabilities before ensembling
nodes.principle: After fine-tuning, optimize a temperature parameter on the validation set to scale logits before softmax, improving probability calibration and ensemble performance.
nodes.condition: When transformer probabilities are overconfident or poorly calibrated, degrading ensemble results.

nodes.title: Use Vision Transformer (ViT) with partial unfreezing and MixUp for cactus classification
nodes.principle: Use a pretrained ViT-Base/16 backbone from timm, unfreeze the last 6 transformer blocks, and add a custom MLP classifier head. Apply MixUp augmentation (50% probability). Use differential learning rates (backbone 1e-5, head 3e-4), AdamW optimizer, cosine annealing scheduler, mixed precision, and early stopping. Use test-time augmentation (horizontal flip averaging) for final predictions.
nodes.condition: When wanting to leverage Vision Transformer architectures for aerial cactus identification with moderate computational resources.

nodes.title: Avoid passing early_stopping_rounds to XGBClassifier.fit() in newer XGBoost versions
nodes.principle: In newer XGBoost versions, do not pass 'early_stopping_rounds' as a parameter to fit(). Instead, use callbacks or the eval_set parameter with early_stopping_rounds in the XGBClassifier constructor.
nodes.condition: When using XGBoost with early stopping in versions >=1.6.

nodes.title: Combine multiple frozen transformer embeddings with XGBoost
nodes.principle: Extract [CLS] embeddings from multiple frozen transformers (e.g., DeBERTa-v3-base, RoBERTa-base, DistilBERT-base), concatenate them, and train an XGBoost classifier with stratified 5-fold cross-validation and early stopping.
nodes.condition: When aiming for high performance without fine-tuning, leveraging diverse representations.

nodes.title: Re-register EMA after unfreezing backbone layers
nodes.principle: When using Exponential Moving Average (EMA) with two-stage fine-tuning, re-register EMA parameters after unfreezing backbone layers to include newly trainable parameters in the shadow dictionary.
nodes.condition: When using EMA with staged unfreezing where backbone parameters become trainable after initial registration.

nodes.title: Use weighted ensemble averaging of transformer predictions
nodes.principle: Average the softmax probabilities from multiple fine-tuned transformers (e.g., 0.5 DistilBERT + 0.5 RoBERTa) to produce final predictions; tune weights on validation set.
nodes.condition: When individual transformer models show complementary strengths and overfitting patterns.

nodes.title: Use DeBERTa-v3-large with standard AutoModelForSequenceClassification for strong performance
nodes.principle: Use microsoft/deberta-v3-large with HuggingFace's AutoModelForSequenceClassification, CLS pooling, dropout, and linear classifier, fine-tuned with AdamW, cosine schedule, label smoothing, gradient clipping, and early stopping.
nodes.condition: When aiming for high accuracy on text classification tasks with sufficient GPU memory.

nodes.title: Use Focal Loss with label smoothing for imbalanced text classification
nodes.principle: Use Focal Loss (gamma=2.0) combined with label smoothing (epsilon=0.1) to handle class imbalance and prevent overconfidence. Apply with AdamW optimizer and gradient clipping.
nodes.condition: When dealing with class imbalance in multi-class text classification.

nodes.title: Use 5-fold stratified cross-validation with ensemble averaging for robust predictions
nodes.principle: Split training data into 5 stratified folds. For each fold, train a model on 4 folds and validate on the held-out fold, using early stopping to prevent overfitting. Average predictions from all folds for the test set.
nodes.condition: When building a robust model for small-to-medium datasets, needing to reduce variance, and having sufficient compute time.

nodes.title: Avoid leaving stray text comments outside of comment blocks in Python code
nodes.principle: Ensure all explanatory text is inside comments (#) or docstrings. Remove any lines that are not valid Python code before execution.
nodes.condition: When writing or editing Python scripts; stray text causes SyntaxError.

nodes.title: Use DistilRoBERTa with weighted averaging of last 4 hidden states and deep classification head
nodes.principle: Use DistilRoBERTa backbone with weighted average of last 4 hidden states, mean pooling, and a deep classification head with LayerNorm and dropout. Train with CrossEntropyLoss with label smoothing, AdamW optimizer, mixed precision, and gradient clipping.
nodes.condition: When using DistilRoBERTa for text classification and needing better representation than CLS token.

nodes.title: Ensure model forward method returns logits consistently for evaluation
nodes.principle: Define model forward to return a tuple (logits, pooled) or a single tensor. Ensure evaluate() function unpacks the correct number of outputs. Avoid multiple evaluate() definitions that expect different return signatures.
nodes.condition: When implementing custom model forward and evaluation loops; mismatched return signatures cause runtime errors.

nodes.title: Use progressive unfreezing with discriminative learning rates and stochastic depth for transformer fine-tuning
nodes.principle: Gradually unfreeze transformer layers from top to bottom, applying lower learning rates to lower layers. Use stochastic depth regularization on top layers. Train with AdamW optimizer, linear warmup, and early stopping.
nodes.condition: When fine-tuning a transformer model and needing to prevent catastrophic forgetting and overfitting.

nodes.title: Define all classes and functions before their first use in the script
nodes.principle: Order code so that class and function definitions appear before any instantiation or call. For test datasets, define the dataset class before creating test loaders.
nodes.condition: When writing Python scripts with custom classes; NameError occurs if used before definition.

nodes.title: Use DeBERTa-v3-large with mean pooling, multi-sample dropout, and Focal Loss for robust text classification
nodes.principle: Use DeBERTa-v3-large backbone with mean pooling of hidden states, multi-sample dropout (4 samples), and a simple linear classifier head. Train with Focal Loss (gamma=2.0), AdamW optimizer, mixed precision (AMP), gradient clipping, linear warmup, and ReduceLROnPlateau scheduler. Use 5-fold stratified cross-validation and early stopping.
nodes.condition: When performing text classification with a transformer model and needing strong regularization to prevent overfitting, or when fine-tuning DeBERTa-v3-large for a stable baseline.
